Description:

**Supervisor’s Title: Chief Financial Officer**

**Exempt Status: Exempt**

**Location: Must be able to work at the Burnsville Location**

**Compensation:** The expected salary/wage for this Minnesota-based position is between $130,000 -$180,000. This range represents a good faith estimate for this position. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s knowledge, skills, and or experience. In addition, this position may be eligible for a range of benefits (e.g., Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Accounts, Health Care & Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts, Disability Benefits, Life Insurance, and Retirement Benefits).

**Basic Function**

The IT Manager will serve as Imricor’s senior IT professional, with responsibility for information technology operations, business systems, cybersecurity, and technology improvement initiatives. This role will oversee the external managed service provider (MSP), which will remain responsible for primary service-desk and day-to-day technical support, while ensuring reliable, secure, scalable, and user-focused service delivery. The IT Manager will also lead IT projects, strengthen IT controls and documentation, and partner with business leaders on technology decisions. This position is expected to grow in scope as Imricor expands its internal technology capabilities and business systems environment. This position is responsible for complying with the Quality System requirements and carrying out responsibilities as outlined in the environmental, health, and safety policies.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads the execution of Imricor’s IT strategy, roadmap, priorities, and improvement initiatives in alignment with Company objectives, growth plans, risk profile, and budget.
* Serves as the primary internal owner of IT operations, business systems, cybersecurity, end-user technology, enterprise AI governance, and related policies, procedures, and documentation.
* Oversees the Company’s external managed service provider (MSP), including service delivery, help-desk performance, ticket trends, user experience, escalations, service expectations, and continuous-improvement activities.
* Partners with business leaders to assess technology needs, recommend solutions, prioritize projects, and support the effective use of Company technology platforms.
* Oversees identity and access management; technology onboarding and offboarding; device, software, and asset lifecycle management; and related vendor, licensing, and procurement activities.
* Leads implementation and ongoing monitoring of the Information and Data Processing Security Policy, including related controls, procedures, documentation, and remediation activities.
* Partners with the MSP and internal stakeholders to maintain, test, and improve incident-response, disaster-recovery, backup, and business-continuity processes.
* Other relevant duties as assigned.

Requirements:

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology or related field.
* 7-10 years of progressively responsible, hands-on IT experience, including IT operations, infrastructure, end-user technology, business applications, cybersecurity, and project delivery.
* Demonstrated experience serving as a primary IT resource or senior technical lead in a small or mid-sized organization, with the ability to operate independently and manage competing priorities with limited oversight.
* Experience with IT asset management, hardware and software lifecycle planning, SaaS administration, licensing, technology procurement, and vendor management.
* Experience in a public company or similarly controlled environment.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain technical information to nontechnical users, managers, and senior leadership.
* Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

**Working Conditions**

* Light work, exerting up to 20 lbs. of force or less.
* Requires clarity of vision at 20 inches or less (near vision) and ability to identify/distinguish colors.
* Requires finger manipulation, repetitive motion, talking and hearing.
* 85% of time requires viewing and working at computer screen.
* Significant work pace & pressure due to deadlines.

The statements above reflect the principal function and most significant duties of the job as necessary for its evaluation in relation to other jobs in the organization and shall not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be inherent in the job. Any functions that are non-Essential will be identified as such above. A request for Reasonable Accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Vice Chancellor and General Counsel**

The Office of the Chancellor of the California State University System (CSU), the largest, most diverse, and most consequential university system in the United States, seeks a highly skilled and experienced leader to serve as Vice Chancellor and General Counsel (VC and GC).

**The California State University System**

The CSU’s 22 universities across California enroll nearly 500,000 diverse students, making it the world’s largest four-year public higher education system. More than half of CSU students are from traditionally underrepresented backgrounds, and more than one-quarter of undergraduates are first-generation college students. Because the CSU’s 22 universities provide a high-quality education at an incredible value, they are rated among the best in the nation for promoting social mobility from U.S. News & World Report, the Wall Street Journal, and Washington Monthly.

With universities stretching from Humboldt in the north to San Diego in the south, the CSU System provides affordable, high-quality education to meet California’s evolving workforce needs. To learn more about the CSU, visit our site.

The Office of General Counsel (OGC) provides, manages and coordinates all legal services for the California State University. The General Counsel is the chief legal officer with full authority and responsibility for the legal affairs of the institution. This includes providing representation and advice to the Board of Trustees, the Chancellor, university leaders, and all 22 CSU campuses. The General Counsel approves the retention of outside counsel and has authority over the resolution of claims. In addition, the General Counsel also serves as secretary of the Board of Trustees. The OGC is a collaborative, problem-solving team of 37 attorneys and 16 support staff committed to providing excellent service and support. The office develops proactive partnerships with campus and systemwide clients, working closely with them to understand and achieve their objectives while minimizing risk and cost. The OGC helps the CSU meet emerging challenges while advancing its commitment to educational opportunity, equity, academic excellence and public service. Departments within and services provided by the OGC include:

**Legal Services** – Legal services are centralized to facilitate and streamline the efficient delivery of consistent advice. Within this framework, each university is assigned a dedicated university counsel who manages all legal affairs for that university. In addition to making regular campus visits, university counsel interacts daily with the president’s cabinet and other campus leadership to support their work. University counsel also manages all litigation arising out of their assigned university. Five full-time litigators handle all types of litigation in all types of venues. The litigators also handle administrative hearings involving employee discipline or dismissal, and arbitrations concerning the denial of tenure or promotion for faculty.

**OGC Attorneys** – Attorneys are assigned to one of six OGC teams – Business & Finance, Civil Rights, External Affairs, Human Resources, Litigation, and Student Success & Academic Affairs – to better serve the functional divisions in the Office of the Chancellor. OGC attorneys are also responsible for developing expertise in areas of law where issues arise with enough frequency to warrant specialized skill within the OGC. These specialty areas include the First Amendment, athletics, California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), information security, collective bargaining, discrimination and harassment, disability accommodation, student fees, contracts and procurement, Public Records Act requests, open meetings laws, Title IX, intellectual property, and tax issues. Deputy General Counsel assists General Counsel with the day-to-day management of the OGC, provides systemwide and campus-based legal advice on a variety of legal issues and serves as the assistant secretary to the Board of Trustees.

**About the Position**

The Vice Chancellor and General Counsel reports directly to the Chancellor of the CSU and has a dotted line report to the Board of Trustees. As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VC and GC provides strategic legal leadership and counsel to the Chancellor, Board of Trustees, and senior executives across the CSU as the System’s chief legal officer. The VC and GC also serves as Secretary to the Board of Trustees and is responsible for Board process, including compliance with the Open Meeting Act. description:
**Chief Financial Officer**

The Northern Indiana Commuter Transportation District (NICTD), operator of the South Shore Line Railroad, is seeking an experienced financial executive leader to serve as Chief Financial Officer (CFO). The CFO is the District's senior financial executive and a principal advisor to the President and General Manager, executive leadership team, and Board of Trustees. The CFO is accountable for the integrity, transparency, efficiency, and long-term sustainability of NICTD's financial operations and for aligning operating and capital resources with the safe, reliable delivery of South Shore Line service.

This is both a stewardship and transformation role. The CFO will maintain disciplined governmental accounting, grant, audit, treasury, debt, payroll, procurement, and internal-control practices while leading the modernization of financial systems, data, workflows, and management reporting. The successful candidate will understand the operational and financial realities of a public railroad, including collectively bargained labor, around-the-clock service, federally funded capital programs, multiple governmental funding partners, and public accountability.

**Executive Mandate:**

* Give the President and General Manager and Board timely, candid, decision-ready analysis - not simply historical financial reports.
* Protect public funds and funding eligibility through reliable controls, compliant records, accurate reporting, and prompt correction of audit or grant findings.
* Lead the District's transition from operating primarily under a business plan to preparing, adopting, and managing against a formal annual operating and capital budget, supported by a multi-year financial forecast.
* Modernize the finance function through an enterprise roadmap for core financial, payroll, timekeeping, procurement, grants, budgeting, asset, and reporting systems, with disciplined change management and uninterrupted business continuity.
* Develop a capable, accountable finance organization with documented processes, cross-training, succession depth, service standards, and measurable performance.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**
Financial Strategy, Business Planning and Executive Advice

* Serve as the President and General Manager's principal financial advisor; identify emerging risks, tradeoffs, and opportunities and recommend clear courses of action.
* Design and execute a disciplined transition from the District's current business-plan process to a formal annual operating and capital budget process, while retaining a multi-year business plan as a strategic forecasting and policy tool.
* Establish a budget calendar, revenue and expenditure assumptions, departmental instructions, position and labor-cost controls, capital programming standards, executive review, Board adoption, amendment authority, and clear ownership for every material budget line.
* Administer the adopted budget through monthly budget-to-actual reporting, rolling forecasts, variance explanations, expenditure and position controls, and timely corrective-action plans developed with accountable department heads.
* Integrate the annual budget with cash flow, grants, debt obligations, reserves, capital commitments, ridership and fare revenue, collective bargaining obligations, and multi-year operating and capital forecasts.
* Translate complex financial matters for the Board, elected and appointed officials, funding partners, employees, labor representatives, auditors, lenders, and the public through clear written reports and presentations.
* Establish useful financial and operational performance indicators and lead recurring variance reviews with department heads; require corrective action when results depart materially from plan.
* Evaluate service, workforce, procurement, project, and investment proposals for full life-cycle cost, funding eligibility, affordability, risk, and measurable return to the District.

Accounting, Reporting, Controls and Audit

* Direct general accounting, accounts payable and receivable, payroll accounting, capital assets, revenue accounting, cost allocation, financial close, and preparation of audited financial statements.
* Ensure compliance with GAAP, GASB standards, applicable Indiana requirements, the National Transit Database Uniform System of Accounts, federal award requirements, District policy, debt covenants, and other governing requirements.
* Maintain a practical, risk-based system of internal controls, segregation of duties, delegations of authority, reconciliations, documentation, fraud prevention, and records retention.
* Lead relationships with external auditors and oversight bodies; ensure timely, accurate responses and durable corrective action on findings and management recommendations.
* Maintain financial continuity and recovery plans for critical functions, including payroll, cash, vendor payments, grant drawdowns, and financial reporting.

* Ensure compliance with GAAP, GASB standards, applicable Indiana requirements, the National Transit Database Uniform System of Accounts, federal award requirements, District policy, debt covenants, and other governing requirements.
* Maintain a practical, risk-based system of internal controls, segregation of duties, delegations of authority, reconciliations, documentation, fraud prevention, and records retention.
* Lead relationships with external auditors and oversight bodies; ensure timely, accurate responses and durable corrective action on findings and management recommendations.
* Maintain financial continuity and recovery plans for critical functions, including payroll, cash, vendor payments, grant drawdowns, and financial reporting.

**ABOUT THE AGENCY**

Chartered in 1834, the Long Island Rail Road (LIRR) is the largest, busiest, and oldest continuously operating commuter railroad in the United States. In 2024, this 24/7/365 operation served 75.5 million riders on a system that stretches nearly 120 miles – from Penn Station and Grand Central Madison in Manhattan to Montauk on the eastern tip of Long Island.

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Chief Program Officer – Special Projects position is the Program Executive accountable for directing the LIRR Interface and management activities associated with the East Side Access (ESA), Penn Station Improvements (PSI) Penn Station Access (PSA), Moynihan, Westside Yard (WSY) Overbuild, Western and Eastern Rail Yards (WRY & ERY) and other Special Projects.

The Chief Program Officer – Special Projects, as the program executive, has executive responsibility and business, legal, operational, and technical authority for overseeing the implementation and management of the LIRR's Capital and assigned Operating Funded Projects to ensure scope, schedule and budget adherence. The Chief Program Officer – Special Projects ensures the coordination of all policy, business, legal, construction, operations, activities related to the design construction and opening of several multi-billion-dollar projects. The Chief Program Officer leads the teams that directs the LIRR Force Account construction and construction support activities. This includes the development of an overall business plan and schedule of milestones to ensure all operational staffing needs, budgetary requirements, legal agreements, procurements, hiring and training of new hires, and technical issues are addressed and resolved.

The Chief Program Officer represents LIRR on multiple Mega and Special Projects, coordinates with regional special projects, and will cultivate relationships with key internal and external stakeholders throughout the new MTA organization and the industry to support effective planning, development, and delivery of major investments of the LIRR's operating infrastructure.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Oversee the direction and coordination of all LIRR Special Projects construction and third-party construction support activities; lead LIRR efforts to effectively identify, track and resolve all technical engineering issues; facilitation of design resources with LIRR operating department participation, reviews and decision-making.
* Ensure support of all construction by managing LIRR processes and forces required for submittal reviews, issue resolution, inspection and testing for all third-party construction.
* Direct LIRR involvement in the management of activities associated with overbuilds and special projects, including interfaces with all LIRR Departments. Major overbuilding/development projects include the 9th Avenue and Hudson Yard Development Projects; Special Projects include Moynihan, Gateway, NYCT 7 Line Extension and Penn Plaza/Penn Station.
* Serve as LIRR’s lead in negotiations with Developers on construction agreements including the major overbuild projects and Atlantic Yards Real Estate at Penn Station.
* Direct the management and coordination of the development, planning, review and implementation of a variety of Penn Station Projects including joint projects with Amtrak and 3rd. party consultants/contractors engaged in technical studies, design and construction. Overall responsibility for the cost and schedule control of projects assigned.
* Represent LIRR as the program executive
* Ensure alignment of all LIRR Special Projects with long range goals. Provide the management and control of the Program.
* Monitor and interpret legislative trends, proposals and actions to ensure that the LIRR’s interests are protected.
* Ensure required interaction among the Rail Road, MTA States Agencies and FTA to provide the necessary funding for various operating and capital needs.
* Represents LIRR as Program Executive to:

* Facilitate project activities

* Resolve policy and technical issues between LIRR and projects

* Provide leadership for achievement of department goals and objectives, and the management and coordination of business administrative activities to ensure the Long Island Rail Road (LIRR) is prepared for the open

**Description**

**Job Title:**Senior Project Manager, Tolling Operations

**Resume Due Date:** October 22,2026

**Department****:** Tolling Operations

**Work Location:**Randalls Island

**Job Family/ Grade:** PPM007

**Earnings Potential:**$93,369- $117,144

MTA Bridges and Tunnels reserves the right to remove this posting before the application deadline.

MTA Bridges and Tunnels operates the largest bridge and tunnel network in New York City, managing nine crossings that include seven bridges and two tunnels. Serving more than 336 million vehicle crossings each year, this network connects communities across the five boroughs and supports regional mobility. In addition, MTA Bridges and Tunnels oversees the Congestion Relief Zone, working to ensure safe, efficient travel and a more sustainable urban environment. MTA strives to provide a safe and reliable commute, excellent customer service, and rewarding opportunities.

**Telework:**

This position is eligible for telework which is currently one day per week. New hires are eligible to apply 30 days after their effective date of hire.

**Job Summary:**

The Senior Project Manager is responsible for delivering complex technology and infrastructure projects supporting tolling and revenue collection operations. Defines project scope, manages cross-functional teams, and ensures project deliverables meet established goals within project timelines and budget constraints. The position will work on large-scale tolling projects, including the Back Office, Central Business District Tolling, and Open Road Tolling programs, as well as non-tolling systems such as Work Zone Speed Enforcement, Weigh in Motion, Revenue Recovery, and other complex, high-visibility projects. The complexity and scale of these projects require strong project management skills, in-depth knowledge of tolling and ITS, and an understanding of public-sector procurement processes. The position will also be responsible for developing Requests for Proposals (RFPs), coordinating procurement activities, and managing multiple consultant teams throughout project delivery.

**Responsibilities:**

* Deliver complex technology and infrastructure tolling projects by managing project resources, schedules, deliverables, and timelines to achieve established project objectives.
* Define project scope, goals, deliverables, and requirements for complex tolling and technology infrastructure projects.
* Develop and manage comprehensive project plans, including resource requirements, risk assessment and mitigation strategies, schedules, and project milestones.
* Facilitate effective communication and coordination among internal stakeholders, external partners, and consultants involved in tolling system implementations, including coordination of procurement activities and consultant deliverables.
* Monitor project performance, identify issues and potential impacts, and provide project status reports and recommendations to stakeholders.
* Ensure project activities comply with applicable regulations, standards, policies, and requirements related to tolling technologies and infrastructure.
* Performs other duties as assigned
* Complies with all policies and standards
* May be required to work hours outside regular work hours, as applicable
* Observes the work performed by contractors, as applicable
* Reviews invoices and approves them if the work has contractual standards, as applicable
* Addresses performance issues with the contractor when possible, as applicable
* Escalates issues to other parties when needed, as applicable

**Qualification****s****:**

Bachelor’s degree in arts/sciences (BA/BS) in Project Management, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field.

An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered

Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience managing complex technology, infrastructure, systems implementation, or similar projects.

Demonstrated working knowledge managing complex projects, including project scope, resources, schedules, deliverables, and timelines.

Demonstrated working knowledge managing and coordinating resources, project teams, consultants, or contractors.

Demonstrated working knowledge integrating technology systems or managing technology-related projects.

Demonstrated working knowledge with infrastructure development, Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), tolling systems, transportation technology, or other complex operational technology environments.

Demonstrated working knowledge coordinating technical teams and stakeholders across multiple functional areas.

Unrestricted driver's license in New York State.

**Preferred****:**

Master’s degree in arts/scienc

**Job Description**
-------------------

**Position Purpose:**

This is an 18-to-24-month rotational leadership opportunity to support the Chief Procurement Officer and Interim Head of Supply Chain. Reporting into the Chief Procurement Officer (CPO), the Procurement Director, Decision Support Lead (DSL) will support the CPO and Leadership Team in formulating and driving execution of the procurement strategic roadmap and key enterprise procurement initiatives. The DSL will also support the CPO, who is serving as the interim Head of Supply Chain, to manage key initiatives and forums with the Supply Chain organization in support of the Supply Chain strategic roadmap.

Experience in this role will give the DSL enterprise-wide exposure, executive decision-making experience, and options to transition into high-visibility roles upon successful completion of the rotation.

**Work Environment:**

**\\*\\*\\* This is a hybrid position based onsite at any of the posted locations with a minimum of 3 days onsite weekly. Relocation and mobility assistance are not provided.**

**Overview:**

* Recognized as leading expert in area of expertise, tasked with managing complex project initiatives of strategic importance to the organization

* Recommend operational strategies and plans with direct impact on overall functional results

* Manages Procurement’s strategic roadmap aligned to its vision, mission and strategic priorities

* Requires ability to influence others to adopt new practices and approaches, and ability to influence executive leadership on matters of strategic importance

**Reporting Relationships**
---------------------------

**This role reports to:** Chief Procurement Officer (CPO) & Interim Head of Supply Chain

**Main Responsibilities and Accountabilities**
----------------------------------------------

**1. Organizational Impact:** Recommends or implements operational plans and strategies that will directly impact the achievement of procurement’s functional results. Manages the operational plan and roadmap for procurement activities with short to mid-term impact on results (1-2 years), in direct support of the CPO's strategic roadmap.

**2. Leadership and Talent Management:** Responsible for providing guidance, coaching and training to other employees across the organization within the area of expertise. Responsible for managing complex projects and initiatives of strategic importance to the organization, involving multiple interfaces and cross-functional teams.

**3. Communication and Influence:** Communicates with parties within and outside the Procurement function, including responsibilities for communicating with parties external to the organization, which may include suppliers, partners, or customers. Works to influence others to adopt new concepts, practices and approaches. Frequently conducts briefings to senior leaders both inside and outside Procurement, in support of the CPO’s quarterly stakeholder engagements.

**4. Innovation and Complexity:** Responsible for improving upon existing processes and systems, using significant conceptualizing, reasoning and interpretation. Solutions are novel and unique and draw upon best practices based on expertise. Problems and issues faced are complex, requiring broad-based consideration of variables that impact multiple areas of the organization. description:
#### **Join Axon and be a Force for Good.**

At Axon, we're on a mission to Protect Life. We're explorers, pursuing society's most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you'll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

**Your Impact**
---------------

Axon's Productivity Team is transforming Corrections by giving officers time back, strengthening investigations, and accelerating justice with the first AI-era productivity suite for correctional officers, investigators and leadership. As a Strategic Account Executive, you'll lead that revolution.

As a Strategic Account Executive on Axon's Productivity Team, you will lead high-stakes, consultative sales efforts with the largest Corrections agencies in the U.S. This role goes beyond traditional RMS sales — you will bring together Axon Records, Axon Standards, and Axon's rapidly expanding suite of AI-powered productivity tools to deliver transformational outcomes for agencies.

This is a quota-carrying, senior-level role that demands precision, creativity, and executive presence. You'll guide Corrections executives, investigators and command staff through the shift from outdated, legacy systems into a future where Axon is the central nervous system of day-to-day Corrections — improving officer productivity, investigation time, and safer outcomes for correctional staff and residents.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

**Location:** Remote, National Role

**Reports to:** Director of Productivity

* **Be a Trusted Advisor:** Act as a strategic partner to executives, investigators, and IT staff advising on how AI-powered productivity solutions can modernize operations and improve correctional safety outcomes.
* **Drive Strategic Deals:** Lead discovery and execution in long-cycle, high-value deals across Records management, Standards, and AI tools; align stakeholders across agencies and shepherd procurement through complex processes.
* **Sell Innovation:** Position Axon's Productivity Suite as the first platform of its kind — an AI-era ecosystem that transforms Corrections from legacy, paper-based processes into "see, respond, report + close, and strengthen."
* **Deliver Impactful Demonstrations:** Lead compelling, scenario-driven demos with support from solution engineers to show how Records and AI unlock measurable staff efficiency and investigative outcomes.
* **Align Internally:** Collaborate across Sales, Product, Professional Services, Legal, and Marketing to ensure customer success from first conversation to final close.
* **Shape the Market:** Represent Axon at regional and national Corrections conferences, contributing to our thought leadership in AI, productivity, and the future of records.
* **Forecast with Precision:** Maintain accurate pipeline and forecast data in Salesforce, while developing territory strategies that build long-term growth and category leadership.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* **Proven Success in Complex Enterprise SaaS Sales** (7+ years) with a track record of exceeding quota in multi-stakeholder, consultative deals.
* **Experience Selling Disruptive Technology** — ideally AI, cloud, or digital transformation solutions in highly regulated industries.
* **Executive Presence & Gravitas:** Able to confidently engage executives, investgators and CIOs with clarity, credibility, and influence.
* **Consultative Expertise:** Adept at uncovering latent customer needs, guiding long-cycle strategies, and aligning solutions to measurable ROI.
* **Public Safety Knowledge (Preferred):** 2+ years selling to or working with law enforcement, Corrections, PSAPs, or justice systems.
* **Startup + Scale Experience:** Comfortable operating in high-growth environments with a balance of autonomy and collaboration.
* **High Travel Flexibility:** Willingness to travel 50% to engage directly with customers and partners across the U.S.

**Benefits that Benefit You**
-----------------------------

* Competitive salary and 401k with employer match
* Discretionary paid time off
* Paid parental leave for all
* Medical, Dental, Vision plans
* Fitness Programs
* Emotional & Mental Wellness support
* Learning & Development programs
* And yes, we have snacks in our offices

*Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work*

Don't meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

* Assist with preparation of corporate resolutions, written consents, secretary and incumbency certificates, good standing certificates, certified organizational documents, and other governance deliverables needed for signing and closing

* Coordinate with Corporate Legal team to support Know Your Customer, beneficial ownership, sanctions, anti-bribery, and other onboarding or counterparty diligence processes related to transactions

Join us today as the Director of Procurement!

First Business Bank is a Top Workplaces USA company, learn more here.

At the heart of First Business Bank, we believe success comes down to putting people first. Our people are our priority — they embody ambition, experience, and client focus. The result is extremely engaged employees who provide unmatched client satisfaction. With comprehensive total rewards to support our team members, a commitment to valuing each other’s differences, and a focus on improving our communities, we are confident you’ll find the experience is your advantage. We’re delighted you’re considering joining us!

**Work Model:** *Remote, requiring one day at our Madison, WI headquarters each month.*

**Position Overview**

The Director of Procurement provides centralized oversight of the Company’s end-to-end procurement-to-payment process. This includes establishing sourcing and vendor strategies aligned with business needs, financial objectives and risk appetite. This is a senior level, individual contributor role with the primary responsibility of building a procure to pay process with an annual spend of approximately $30 million across approximately 300 vendors that can scale as the company grows.

The individual will be expected to foster strong cross-functional collaboration with Finance, Legal, IT, Operations, and business leaders. The position reports to the Chief Risk Officer, with a functional or dotted-line relationship to the Chief Accounting Officer for financial controls, accounts payable integration, and budgeting.

**Essential responsibilities for this role include:**

* **Strategic Sourcing and Procurement (50%).** Develop and lead the company’s strategic sourcing program across key categories of spend through disciplined, transparent, competitive and risk informed processes.
+ Establish and document sourcing standards, including business-case requirements, competitive-bid expectations, exception protocols, and delegated approval authorities.
+ Oversee supplier proposals, bid processes, pricing and business term negotiations.
+ Identify and deliver measurable opportunities for cost savings, cost avoidance, demand management, supplier consolidation, contract optimization, and process efficiency.
+ Coordinate periodic vendor evaluations, risk review and issue resolutions in partnership with Compliance through the lifecycle of the contract.
* **Accounts Payable and Finance Coordination (30%).** The role is responsible for ensuring that procurement and payment processes are efficient, appropriately controlled, supported by complete and accurate records, and executed in accordance with delegated authority.
+ Own and continuously improve the end-to-end P2P process, including requisitioning, vendor payment data maintenance, invoicing, approvals, payment workflows, and the integration of P2P systems.
+ Partner with finance to identify and eliminate bottlenecks, reduce manual work, and improve data quality across purchasing and Accounts Payable processes using key performance indicators.
+ Support Finance and business leaders in vendor-spend forecasting, budget preparation, and accrual identification.
+ Design and monitor controls over vendor creation and changes, purchasing authority, invoice approval, employee expense process, sponsorships process, and documentation standards.
* **Reporting and Analytics (10%).** Establish transparent, decision-useful reporting and performance analytics that enable management of enterprise spend, procurement value, supplier performance, process efficiency, control compliance, and material issues.
+ Develop recurring reporting appropriate to the Company’s governance structure and the significance of procurement, supplier, and P2P matters. Provide trend analysis and actionable recommendations to management.
+ Monitor timely completion of due diligence and periodic reviews; document and escalate overdue items, exceptions, residual risks, control deficiencies, contractual concerns, and significant supplier issues.
+ Establish operational metrics, technology strategy, and staffing models to support efficient, scalable P2P operations.
+ Demonstrate cost savings in procurement program through optimization of vendors, improved contract terms, and reduction of process waste.
* **Governance and Risk Management (10%)**. Administer a risk-based procurement governance framework in partnership with vendor owners, Finance, Legal, Risk and Compliance, Information Security, Information Technology, Operations and business leaders.
+ Define roles and responsibilities for vendor owners, service owners, approvers, Accounts Payable, and oversight functions.
+ Design and maintain controls related to vendor management, purchasing, approvals, and payments.
+ Support regulatory examinations, internal and external audits, and remediation of findings relating to procurement, contracting, and procure-to-pay (“P2P”) processes.

description:
A government professional-services firm is seeking experienced **Senior** **Contract Specialists** to support a potential U.S. Navy contract at a shipyard in Kittery, Maine. This is a **contingent position**, contingent on contract award, government approval, and meeting applicable position requirements.

**Position Overview**

The Senior Contract Specialist will lead advanced acquisition support and quality oversight across the full contract lifecycle for the most complex procurements, and mentor contract specialists. You will also lead pre-award, award, and post-award functions on complex fixed-price and cost-type actions; advanced cost/price analysis and negotiation support; peer review for FAR/DFARS compliance; on-the-job mentoring and knowledge-sharing.

**Required qualifications (PWS §4.2):**

* 8 years of U.S. Government contracting experience (as above)
* **DAWIA Contracting Professional Certification or equivalent — DAWIA Level III, or FAC-C (new)/FAC-C-DoD, or FAC-C Level III (legacy)**
* Bachelor’s degree (Business preferred)
* Expert federal-contracting knowledge; advanced Excel and federal-systems proficiency (as above)
* Demonstrated experience training, mentoring, or knowledge-sharing

Work Location & Schedule

* **Location:** On-site at a U.S. Navy shipyard in Kittery, Maine
* **Employment:** Full-time, W-2
* **Schedule:** Monday through Friday, 8 hours per day
* **Operating Hours:** 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time
* **Telework:** Only when approved by the government

**Eligibility Requirements**

8 years of U.S. Government contracting experience; a specified contracting certification or equivalent; a bachelor's degree; advanced Excel skills; and proficiency in federal acquisition systems.

Candidates must also:

* Be a **U.S. citizen**.
* CAC/DBIDS eligible
* Be able to work **on-site in Kittery, Maine**.

**Security clearance note:** The solicitation references an active security clearance at the time of award. The specific clearance level is currently being confirmed with the Contracting Officer.

**Compensation: $120,000 annually**

Important Notice

**This is a contingent employment opportunity.** Any offer of employment will be contingent upon contract award, government approval, verification of required qualifications and credentials, and satisfaction of applicable security and access requirements.

**Job Type:** Full-time

***Montcure, LLC*** *is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) founded with a vision to revolutionize consulting and advisory services through innovative, data-driven solutions. The Montcure team recognizes the unique challenges faced by organizations and governments in today’s rapidly evolving business environment.*

**Position Description**

The Program Manager - Senior Contract Specialist provides overall program leadership and senior-level federal acquisition support for DOE/NNSA. This position is responsible for the management and oversight of contractor and subcontractor personnel while also supporting complex cradle-to-grave acquisition, contract administration, cost-type contract closeout, and procurement activities.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide program management and oversight for all contractor and subcontractor activities performed under the assigned task order.
* Serve as a primary contractor in interface with the Government Contracting Officer (CO) and Contracting Officer Representative (COR) for performance, staffing, and day-to-day contract matters.
* Monitor workforce productivity, quality, staffing continuity, workload distribution, and overall contract performance.
* Provide acquisition support, including pre-solicitation, solicitation, evaluation, award, post-award administration, modification, and closeout activities.
* Support acquisition planning, market research, source-selection documentation, proposal evaluation, cost/price analysis, negotiation support, and contract award documentation.
* Provide general and cost-type contract closeout support, including reconciliation of audit information, de-obligation actions, and expired cost-type contract support.
* Prepare recurring program status reports, identify risks or performance issues, recommend corrective actions, and keep Government stakeholders informed.
* Ensure acquisition and contract management activities comply with applicable FAR, RFO, DEAR, agency policies, procedures, and guidance.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
* Minimum of 7 years of contracting experience.
* Experience performing senior contracting functions, including cradle-to-grave acquisition support.
* Experience with general contract closeout and cost-type contract closeout procedures.

* Experience with pre-award, solicitation, post-award, contract administration, and modification activities.
* Minimum of 1 year of program management experience.
* Candidate must be able to comply with DOE/NNSA security, badging, nondisclosure, information protection, and facility-access requirements applicable to the assigned work.
* Candidates must be able to work effectively in a high-volume, complex federal environment and produce accurate, timely, professional work products.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with STRIPES, STARS, FAST, I-MANAGE/IDW, AMIS/PRISM, FedConnect, CPARS/SAM, and Microsoft 365.
* Experience supporting NNSA Headquarters, NA-PAS, DNN, or other NNSA program offices.
* Active DOE L or Q clearance is strongly preferred.

**Travel**

This role may require travel to other DOE/NNSA, or operational sites based on assigned tasking and Government mission requirements.

**Status:** Contingency – This work is contingent upon award.

**Salary Range**: $120-$150k per year

Montcure, LLC does not discriminate* *on the basis of* *race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided* *on the basis of* *qualifications, merit, and business* *need**.*

description:
DomainTools is looking for an experienced **Public Sector Account Director** to accelerate growth by acquiring new government customers across Federal, State and Local, and Education (FED/SLED) markets. This is an individual contributor "hunter" role with no direct reports, who is the quarterback of the Public Sector team responsible for managing a defined public sector territory and achieving bookings targets,The ideal candidate is an accomplished government sales professional with a proven track record of selling into complex federal, state and municipal accounts, and building trusted relationships with executive, program, technical, and procurement stakeholders across public-sector organizations.

The Public SectorAccount Director will own the full-cycle new business sales process within assigned target agencies and institutions, including:from outbound prospecting, identifying, and qualifying opportunities, expanding DomainTools existing footprint through to developing business cases, navigating procurement and contracting requirements, and closing net-new business.

This role requires close partnership across Sales Development, Sales Engineering, Sales Operations, Marketing, Partner Alliances, Product, and our Executive Team. Strong cross-functional influence, communications and orchestration are essential to success.

The successful candidate will combine strategic territory planning, operational rigor, executive presence, consultative selling skills, deep familiarity with government procurement, and a relentless hunter mentality to deliver consistent new business acquisition and predictable business results.

**Key Responsibilities**

**New Business Revenue and Territory Ownership**

* Own the net-new revenue target and sales quota for an assigned Public Sector territory and target agency/institution list.
* Identify, develop, and close new revenue opportunities across DomainTools' government ICP, including federal civilian and defense agencies, state and local governments.Develop and execute strategic territory plans that prioritize the highest-potential agencies, institutions, and target organizations based on mission need, budget cycle, and contract vehicle access.

**ContactPoint360 is looking for a Chief Revenue Officer.**

Not a caretaker.

Not an administrator.

Not someone to preside over a sales organization and explain why the number was missed.

We are looking for someone who can build.

***The mandate is clear:***

**$15 million in new-logo billable revenue every year.**

Not ACV.

Not TCV.

Not pipeline.

Not bookings that may become revenue three years from now.

**Actual revenue.**
**Actually billed.**
**From companies that were not clients before we won them.**

That is the standard.

**The Assignment**

You will lead a focused team of approximately four enterprise salespeople.

Your job is to turn that team into a new-logo growth machine.

Four people.

One leader.

One number.

**$15 million.**

You will own the entire system required to produce it:

**Markets.**
**Accounts.**
**People.**
**Pipeline.**
**Executive access.**
**Deal strategy.**
**Solutions.**
**Pricing.**
**Negotiation.**
**Closing.**
**Launch.**
**Revenue.**

You will not own existing-account farming.

You will not be rewarded for protecting inherited revenue.

You will not spend your time celebrating renewals that would have happened without you.

Your job is to create revenue that did not exist before you arrived.

**We Care About What Is Real**

Sales organizations have developed an extraordinary ability to manufacture the appearance of progress.

More pipeline.

More meetings.

More conferences.

More proposals.

More CRM activity.

More slides explaining why the deal slipped.

None of those things are revenue.

We care about the things that eventually become undeniable:

**A new client signs.**
**The program launches.**
**The client gets billed.**
**ContactPoint360 gets paid.**

Everything before that matters only because it leads to that outcome.

**This Is a Player-Coach Role**

If you believe the job of a CRO is to sit above the sales team and inspect dashboards, this is not the role.

You will be in the arena.

When the team needs executive access, help create it.

When a deal is stuck, get involved.

When pricing needs to be challenged, challenge it.

When a client needs conviction from leadership, show up.

When the solution is not strong enough, make it stronger.

When a salesperson is struggling, coach them.

When the wrong person is in the seat, make the decision.

Leadership here means accountability without distance.

**The Revenue Target**

The annual target is:

**$15,000,000 in NEW-LOGO BILLABLE REVENUE**

The definition matters.

If we sign a five-year contract worth $50 million and only $3 million is billed during the year, the scoreboard shows:

**$3 million.**

If an existing client expands by $10 million, that may be excellent for the company.

But it does not count toward this number.

The CRO owns **new companies entering ContactPoint360 and generating billable revenue.**

That distinction is intentional.

We want the organization obsessed not merely with signing deals, but with:

**When does it launch?**
**How quickly does it ramp?**
**How much revenue will actually be billed this year?**

Revenue delayed is revenue that cannot help us hit the number.

**Your Team**

You will manage approximately four enterprise hunters.

We expect a very high standard.

Every seller should know:

**Which accounts matter.**
**Who the decision makers are.**
**What problem we are solving.**
**What the next step is.**
**What could kill the deal.**
**When the deal will close.**
**When the program will launch.**
**How much revenue it will bill this year.**

A sales leader should be able to look at the pipeline and know which opportunities are real.

Not because the CRM says so.

Because they understand the customer, the politics, the economics and the probability of execution.

**New Logos Only**

This role exists to create new relationships.

We want someone who knows how to enter a company where ContactPoint360 has:

**No contract.**
**No incumbent position.**
**No guaranteed meeting.**
**No inherited relationship.**

And change that.

You should know how to earn access to senior executives.

You should know how to create relevance before an RFP exists.

You should know how to turn a first conversation into a strategic opportunity.

And you should know how to turn that opportunity into revenue.

**Who You Will Sell To**

You should be comfortable operating with:

**CEOs**
**COOs**
**CIOs**
**Chief Customer Officers**

**Chief Experience Officers**
**Transformation Leaders**
**Shared Services Leaders**
**Procurement Executives**

You should understand that complex enterprise sales are rarely won by convincing one person.

The economics.

The risk.

The urgency.

And the people who can say yes or no.

description:
**Department**
--------------

University Business Administrators - College of Music

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

Responsible for performing professional fiscal activities at the College of Music (CoM), including travel, purchasing, and deposit accounting, with an emphasis on student-facing financial functions, including student group travel and tours, student travel grants, scholarships, course-enhancement initiatives, tuition waivers, and student finance communications.

* Responsible for day-to-day origination of travel authorizations, cash advances, and expense reports for student travel, including individual, small group, and large group trips/tours. Provides recommendations to support the travel initiatives developed to enhance and enrich the CoM student experience.
* Creates and maintains CoM-specific travel training guides, travel resources, and post-travel forms. Proactively communicates with International Travel, Safety, and Risk, and the University Clery Compliance Officer prior to CoM group travel.
* Routes student travel waivers prior to departure for all college-sanctioned student group travel. Reviews travel card transactions for accuracy and policy compliance. Maintains appropriate travel logs and regularly updates interested parties on the status of their upcoming travel and post-travel expense reports.
* Tracks and monitors purchasing activities at the CoM to ensure a sound environment of internal controls and compliance. Interprets and communicates policies to faculty, staff, and students. Makes recommendations regarding purchasing processes and advises on alternatives as needed, in particular to accommodate requests for purchase of course materials or in support of student entrepreneurial initiatives.
* Prepares and utilizes college-wide reports for tracking requisitions and purchase orders to ensure adherence to area budget allocations as well as timely transaction entry and payment processing. Communicates with internal stakeholders as necessary and ensures compliance with University policies and procedures.
* Serves as primary PCard holder for CoM Fiscal Office requests. Serves as backup to Sr. Accounting Specialist for faculty, staff, professional development, recruitment, and guest artist travel. Serves as backup PCard Proxy for the CoM, assisting with auditing and coding of departmental purchase card payments as needed. Serves as secondary liaison between College cardholders and FSU Procurement/PCard Admin.
* Enters and reconciles all foundation scholarship awards in FS4U. Collaborates with Sr. Accounting Specialist and Assistant Deans for Admissions & Recruitment and Finance & Administration, as well as the Associate Dean for Academic Affairs, Graduate Academic Program Specialist, and Assistant Dean for Undergraduate Programs to process and reconcile all academic year awards.
* Participates in unencumbered payment activities at the (CoM) to include origination of non-travel reimbursements in FSU Systems, payments to vendors via ePRF, and the PCard program. Identifies process enhancements in existing operations to improve efficiency and delegation throughout the the CoM Fiscal Office.
* Regularly reviews and takes necessary actions on PCard transactions, outstanding T-Card transactions, and aging travel requests, monitoring financial transactions and ensuring compliance with University policy and procedures.
* Serves as a key point of contact for College of Music (CoM) student inquiries pertaining to student financials, including account balances, award disbursements, tuition waivers, insurance subsidies, fee liability, scholarship status, tax liability, payment plans, and adjustments. Serves as a liaison among the CoM Fiscal Office, Office of Student Success, FSU Financial Aid, Student Finance, The Graduate School, and Payroll.

**Qualifications**
------------------

A Bachelor's degree and two years of experience; or a high school diploma or equivalent and six years of experience. (Note: a combination of post high school education and experience equal to six years.)

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

The preferred candidate should have the following skill and/or experience.

* Collaborative attitude and the ability to thrive working with faculty, students, guests, and staff.
* Excellent attention to detail, communication skills, and the ability to work independently.
* Ability to successfully prioritize, organize and perform multiple work assignments simultaneously.

**University Information**
--------------------------

One of the nation's elite research universities, Florida State University preserves, expands, and disseminates knowledge in the sciences, technology, arts, humanities, and professions, while embracing a philosophy of learning strongly rooted in the traditions of the liberal arts and critical thinking. Founded in 1851, Florida State University is the oldest continuous site of higher education in Florida.

description:
**Overview**

The Senior Project Manager – Choice Neighborhoods Implementation Grant leads the project management, coordination, compliance monitoring, performance oversight, and reporting of the Gainesville Housing Authority's Choice Neighborhoods Implementation Grant and related Transformation Plan activities. The position establishes a comprehensive project management and accountability system that provides GHA leadership with current, reliable information on implementation progress, financial status, partner performance, grant requirements, risks, and outcomes.

The Senior Project Manager coordinates GHA departments and external stakeholders to implement the approved Transformation Plan in accordance with HUD requirements, grant agreements, applicable federal regulations, GHA policies, and contractual obligations. The role requires independent judgment, analytical ability, organization, and follow-through.

**Responsibilities**

**Project Management and Software Administration**

* Develop and maintain the Choice Neighborhoods Master Implementation Work Plan including activities, milestones, timelines, dependencies, deliverables, responsible parties, and completion dates.
* Select, configure, implement, or independently administer an approved professional project management platform as GHA's central source of truth for implementation activities.
* Use the platform to assign tasks, monitor completion and overdue activities, maintain project documentation, and integrate the compliance, subrecipient, match, financial, contract, risk, corrective action, and reporting functions described below.
* Conduct regular project status meetings; identify delays, barriers, unresolved issues, and resource needs; and coordinate follow-through with responsible parties.
* Train appropriate GHA staff and partners to use the platform and maintain accurate, current records.

**HUD Grant Compliance**

* Monitor implementation against the grant agreement, approved Transformation Plan,
* HUD requirements, and applicable federal requirements.
* Maintain a consolidated grant compliance and HUD reporting calendar covering required reports, certifications, documentation, milestones, and deliverables; coordinate timely preparation and submission.
* Maintain organized, complete, audit-ready grant records.
* Identify compliance deficiencies, coordinate corrective actions, and track findings from HUD monitoring, audits, reviews, and internal assessments through resolution.

**Subrecipient and Partner Oversight**

* Establish and maintain a Subrecipient Monitoring and Accountability System with a
* master inventory of subrecipients and implementation partners, executed agreements, scopes of work, budgets, and performance and reporting requirements.
* Monitor performance, compliance, deliverables, and deadlines against approved agreements; review performance reports and supporting documentation.
* Coordinate periodic monitoring, document deficiencies, and track corrective actions
* through resolution.
* Ensure subrecipients and partners understand their contractual and grant responsibilities, assignments, reporting requirements, and performance expectations.

**Match and Leveraged Resources**

* Maintain a tracking system for committed and actual match and leveraged resources by, partner, project, funding source, and grant year, including applicable in-kind contributions.
* Monitor outstanding commitments and potential shortfalls; obtain supporting documentation and coordinate verification with Finance.
* Prepare documented match information for internal and HUD reporting, audits, and
* monitoring.

**Budget and Financial Monitoring**

* Work with the Chief Financial Officer and Finance Department to track approved grant and project budgets, obligations, expenditures, remaining funds, and spending timelines.
* Review partner and subrecipient financial reports and expenditures in coordination with Finance.
* Identify budget variances, underutilization, and potential over-expenditure; assist with budget revisions and amendments.
* Maintain project-level financial tracking and accountability while preserving the financial responsibilities of the CFO and Finance Department.

**Contract and Deliverable Tracking**

* Maintain a contract and agreement tracking system covering start and expiration dates, deliverables, renewals, and amendment deadlines.
* Monitor contractor and consultant performance and identify contract performance issues.
* Coordinate with Procurement, Legal, Finance, and appropriate GHA departments; obtain required documentation before closing activities.

**Performance Measurement and Executive Reporting**

* Establish performance measures, collect and analyze data from departments and partners, and monitor progress toward Transformation Plan goals to identify performance gaps.
* Prepare monthly, quarterly, annual, and other required performance reports supported by appropriate documentation; assist with Board presentations

description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

* **Be the offset.** We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.
* **What would it take?** We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.
* **It’s the people.** Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

BENEFITS & PERKS\\*

* **Best-in-class healthcare:** 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options
* **Generous time off:** Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave
* **Fuel for your day:** Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees
* **And more:** 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays
* **Equity participation:** Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

* Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

YOUR MISSION

The Contracts Manager will serve as a senior member of the Prime Contracts Function, personally managing U.S. Department of Defense and Intelligence Community (IC) contracts end to end—from proposal support through award, post-award performance, and closeout. Reporting to the Sr. Contracts Manager, this role will work closely with the proposal and business development team, program managers, and engineering to ensure contracts are properly structured, administered, and closed in compliance with applicable regulations and company policies.

This is a hands-on role in a small, growing legal department. You will carry your own portfolio of contracts from day one, operating with significant autonomy and serving as a direct point of contact with government Contracting Officers and Contracting Officer Representatives. The ideal candidate brings the judgment and initiative that come from working in a lean organization and operating with supervised independence.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

Pre-Award

* Review and analyze RFPs, RFIs, draft solicitations, and other government procurement actions, identifying key terms, risks, and compliance requirements.
* Support proposal development, including preparation of representations and certifications, review of terms and conditions, and input on cost and pricing volumes from a contracts perspective.
* Advise the proposal and business development team on contract structure, risk, and strategy during the capture and proposal process, including educating business development personnel on the advantages, disadvantages, and risk profiles of different contract types (e.g., FFP, CPFF, CPAF, T&M, IDIQ) to support informed pursuit decisions.
* Identify and flag organizational conflicts of interest and other eligibility or compliance considerations during opportunity assessment.

Award and Negotiation

* Review and negotiate contract terms and FAR/DFARS clauses with government Contracting Officers.
* Coordinate internal review and approval of contract documents prior to execution.
* Ensure contracts are properly recorded, distributed, and set up for performance tracking.

Post-Award Administration

* Serve as the primary point of contact with government Contracting Officers and CORs for assigned contracts.
* Manage contract modifications, change orders, option exercises, incremental funding actions, and other post-award contract actions.
* Track and manage CDRLs, deliverable schedules, and other contractual performance obligations.
* Monitor contract performance for scope, funding, and schedule risks, including identification and escalation of issues such as scope creep, constructive changes, and unauthorized commitments.
* Prepare and submit contract correspondence, including cure notices, show cause responses, requests for equitable adjustment, and other formal communications.
* Support claims analysis, preparation, and resolution in coordination with attorneys within the Legal Department.
* Ensure appropriate FAR/DFARS flowdowns in subcontracts and supplier agreements.

Compliance and Audit Support

* Maintain contract files in audit-ready condition in accordance with applicable record retention requirements.
* Serve as the initial point of contact for routine DCAA and DCMA interactions, audits, and information requests.
* Support compliance with cost accounting standards, Truth in Negotiations Act requirements, and other regulatory obligations applicable to government contractors.
* Track and ensure timely completion of compliance-driven reporting and filing obligations tied to contract performance

* **Best-in-class healthcare:** 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options
* **Generous time off:** Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave
* **Fuel for your day:** Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees
* **And more:** 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays
* **Equity participation:** Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

* Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

YOUR MISSION

The Contracts Manager will serve as a senior member of the Prime Contracts Function, personally managing U.S. Department of Defense and Intelligence Community (IC) contracts end to end—from proposal support through award, post-award performance, and closeout. This is a hands-on role in a small, growing legal department. You will carry your own portfolio of contracts from day one, operating with significant autonomy and serving as a direct point of contact with government Contracting Officers and Contracting Officer Representatives. Pre-Award

* Review and analyze RFPs, RFIs, draft solicitations, and other government procurement actions, identifying key terms, risks, and compliance requirements.

* Support compliance with cost accounting standards, Truth in Negotiations Act requirements, and other regulatory obligations applicable to government contractors.

* Full Time
* Houston, TX

**About the Role**

Odyssey Space Research (Odyssey) is seeking a Director of Business Development to own growth in the Civil Space and related commercial space markets. Headquartered in Houston, Odyssey has grown every year for more than two decades into a product and engineering firm of roughly 200 people supporting space mission programs.

The Director identifies, shapes, and captures new business across NASA, other civil agencies, related commercial space companies, and related prime contractor teaming partners. This person leads capture on all qualified opportunities and oversees proposal management from RFP release through submission.

This is a hands-on role with no direct reports (an individual contributor). The Director is expected to personally build relationships, develop win strategies, and drive captures. The position reports to the Chief Growth Officer and works closely with Odyssey’s engineering leadership and subject matter experts to translate technical capability into winning solutions. Supports BD and Capture within other markets as corporate priorities dictate.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Business Development**

* Build and manage a qualified pipeline across NASA (Johnson Space Center and other centers), other civil agencies (e.g., Other NASA Centers, NOAA, FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation), and related commercial space companies.

* Develop and maintain relationships with government program offices, contracting officers, commercial space leaders, and prime contractors.

* Identify and position Odyssey on opportunities early, including recompetes, new starts, SBIR/STTR, and commercial partnerships.

* Shape requirements through customer engagement, RFI and Sources Sought responses, and industry days.

* Run bid/no-bid evaluations and present opportunity qualification to leadership.

* Track market trends, budgets, procurement forecasts, and competitor activity across the civil and commercial space sectors.

* Attend selected conferences and industry events to promote Odyssey and identify opportunities.

**Capture Management**

* Lead capture on all qualified Civil Space and related commercial opportunities.

* Develop win strategies, customer hot buttons, discriminators, and price-to-win inputs.

* Identify, evaluate, and negotiate teaming arrangements with primes and subcontractors, including teaming agreements, product deployment opportunities, and workshare.

* Coordinate solution development with Odyssey engineering leads and subject matter experts.

* Lead capture gate reviews and keep leadership informed of pipeline status.

**Proposal Oversight**

* Oversee proposal management from RFP release through submission, including schedule, compliance, and color team reviews.

* Direct internal contributors and outside proposal support as needed.

* Contribute to key proposal sections such as executive summaries, win themes, and management approach.

* Ensure proposals are compliant, compelling, and submitted on time.

* Lead post-submission activities, including evaluation notice responses, orals preparation, and debriefs.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree.

* 8+ years of experience in business development and/or capture management in the government or space market.

* Demonstrated record of preparing competitive federal contracts as a capture lead.

* Experience overseeing proposals from RFP release through submission.

* Working knowledge of the FAR and federal acquisition processes.

* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including briefing senior customers and executives.

* U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret clearance.

* Ability to work on-site in Houston, TX, and travel approximately 25%.

**Preferred**

* Experience with NASA contract vehicles and procurements (e.g., NASA SEWP, center-level recompetes, SBIR/STTR) and GSA vehicles used by NASA.

* Established relationships within NASA and the commercial space industry.

* Shipley and/or APMP certification.

**What Success Looks Like**

* A qualified, growing Civil Space and commercial pipeline with clear capture plans for priority pursuits.

* Strong customer relationships across NASA centers, civil agencies, and commercial space companies.

* Teaming relationships with primes and partners that position Odyssey to win.

* Compliant, high-quality proposals delivered on schedule, with improving win rates.

This position requires access to information subject to U.S. export control regulations (ITAR/EAR); U.S. citizenship is required.

For over three decades, Cirtec Medical has been a leading outsourcing partner for complex medical devices. We specialize in providing comprehensive solutions for Class II and III devices, from design and development to precision components and finished device assembly. Our expertise spans neuromodulation, implantable drug delivery, cardiac rhythm management, structural heart, mechanical circulatory support, and minimally invasive surgical systems.

Our dedicated teams prioritize growth, innovation, and collaboration. We actively seek opportunities for improvement to enhance our support for clients. If you embrace a growth mindset and thrive on challenges, you may be a perfect fit for our team!

This position is primarily responsible for monitoring and auditing the quality of all manufactured goods in a medical device industry. * Provide Quality Support for the disposition of material via NCR’s.
* Provide Quality Project Management Support as needed for product transfers from validation to production.
* Vendor approval and maintain and assess vendor performance data (i.e. SCAR/on time).
* Review and document procedure changes for quality requirements and compliance with the quality system.

* Audit support for third party audits, customer audits and internal audits.

description:
**About Forterra**

At Forterra, we are unleashing autonomy at scale to transform the battlefield. Our mission is to build the foundational platforms that enable an intelligent ecosystem to coordinate, adapt, and execute with speed and precision even in the uncertainty and disruption of modern conflict. In an era marked by rapid technological change and evolving threats, we design for flexibility, survivability, and operational dominance.

Forterra delivers weapons, sensors, and battlefield effects through integrated autonomous networks reaching operational areas faster, safer, and without placing human lives at risk. Our systems operate with distributed control, dynamic routing, and real-time responsiveness, enabling sustained advantage across complex mission environments.

**About the role**

At Forterra, we're developing the future for Ground Based Autonomy. Forterra is seeking a Senior Software Safety Engineer to join our Safety team and drive efforts in the development of safety-critical autonomous systems. This role is crucial in evolving our Software Development Assurance process, focused on advanced technologies to support our safety assured solutions.

As a Senior Software Safety Engineer, you will be a part of the Core Systems & System Safety team. Our Team is responsible for architecting systems which support safety-critical functions, establishing development methodologies for new technologies, and applying cutting edge hazard analysis techniques.

As part of an experienced multi-disciplinary team, you will contribute to expanding ground based autonomous operational and functional capabilities. Your professional experience in software engineering and system safety will further strengthen the team's ability to support the Warfighter. You will collaborate with members from other groups within Forterra to ensure the safety of innovative solutions for uncrewed ground vehicle operation

**What you'll do**

In your role as a Senior Software Safety Engineer, you will contribute to the development and architectural design supporting the delivery of prototypes and safety-critical ground based autonomous solutions. You will be responsible for performing analyses for hazard identification, evaluation and control using quantitative and qualitative analysis techniques based on the Software System Safety Program Plan and Software Development Plan. You will:

* Work across Forterra to ensure software development processes include safety considerations into our autonomous vehicle systems from the ground up – focusing on defense applications which follow a MIL-STD-882E process.

**Validation & Engineering Group, Inc.** (V&EG) a **Pinnaql** company is a leading services supplier who provides solutions for the Pharmaceutical, Biotechnology, Chemical, Food, and Medical Devices industries in the following areas: Laboratory, Compliance, Computer, Engineering, Project Management, Validation, and other services.

We are seeking a talented, dedicated individual committed to work under the highest ethics standards for the following position:

* Sr CQV Engineer - OSD & SDD

**Job Summary:**
We are seeking a Senior CQV Engineer with a minimum of 10+ years of relevant CQV experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing. The ideal candidate will have strong expertise in Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) manufacturing equipment, including tablet presses, coaters, dispensing systems, and associated manufacturing equipment. Additionally, experience with Spray-Dried Dispersion (SDD) systems, spray dryers, and related process equipment is required. Candidates should have hands-on experience with commissioning, qualification, verification, equipment startup, and technical documentation.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related field.
* **Minimum of 10 years of experience in CQV in the pharmaceutical industry.**
* Proven expertise in OSD and SDD technologies.
* Strong knowledge of tablet presses, coaters, dispensing systems, and spray dryers.
* Experience with equipment startup, commissioning, and qualification processes.
* Ability to provide technical documentation and support across various equipment packages.
* Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.

**Responsibilities:**

* Lead commissioning, qualification, and verification activities for OSD and SDD systems.
* Develop and execute protocols for equipment qualification and validation.
* Conduct equipment startup and troubleshooting as needed.
* Generate and maintain technical documentation following regulatory requirements.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure successful project execution.
* Provide technical expertise and support to ensure compliance with industry standards.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master's degree in Engineering or related field.
* Professional certifications related to CQV in pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Experience with regulatory inspections and audits.
* Familiarity with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP).
* Ability to mentor junior engineers and team members.

At Validation & Engineering Group, people always come first. We believe that when you're empowered to do your best work, bold ideas thrive and real progress happens. This isn't just a job - it's an opportunity to make a meaningful difference by shaping the future of healthcare and technology alongside a purpose-driven, supportive team.

Excited to build something meaningful together? We look forward to hearing from you.

Validation & Engineering Group is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability status.
