* Lead onboarding for agency stakeholders and career staff, translating what they actually need into a rollout plan that survives contact with a live agency.
* Work inside classification and data-handling constraints as a design input, not an obstacle, coordinating closely with engineering on what can be built and how.
* Translate patterns from the field back to Product and Engineering: edge cases, workflow gaps, and the things agencies never put in the RFP but need on day one.
* Act as the connective tissue between customer-facing implementation and the engineers building against Foundry, AIP, and Maven Smart System, so what ships matches what was promised.
* Build the playbooks, templates, and internal documentation that make the next federal deployment faster than this one.
* Guide public sector partners through the actual change management of replacing a legacy system, not just the technical cutover.

**What You'll Bring**
---------------------

* 5+ years in SaaS implementation, onboarding, solutions engineering, or a product-adjacent delivery role (Implementation Consultant, Solutions Architect, Technical Program Manager), with a track record of owning multi-stakeholder rollouts.
* Technical fluency: comfortable working with APIs, data models, and system configurations, and able to hold your own in a conversation with engineers about integration tradeoffs.
* Experience translating customer requirements into implementation plans and technical workflows, not just a status tracker.
* Comfort operating inside classified or otherwise accredited environments, or a clear ability to pick up new compliance and data-handling constraints fast.
* A bias toward action: you'd rather build the process while running the deployment than wait for someone to hand you one.

---------------------------------

* Have deployed software inside a classified or accredited environment before and know where the real friction lives.
* Have worked a program where Palantir was prime, or have hands-on exposure to Foundry, AIP, or Maven Smart System.
* Have touched federal, state, or local government implementation work specifically, versus enterprise SaaS generally.
* Have built implementation playbooks or internal tooling from scratch at an early-stage company.

* Government bureaucracy and slow-moving stakeholders would wear you down instead of something you know how to work with.

description:
Senior Project Manager – Hydroelectric Infrastructure

**Position Overview**

We are seeking an experienced **Senior Project Manager** to lead a large-scale hydroelectric dam maintenance initiative from planning through execution. This highly visible leadership role will oversee critical infrastructure projects that support safe, reliable energy generation and delivery. The successful candidate will collaborate with cross-functional business teams, engineering staff, contractors, consultants, and regulatory agencies to ensure successful project outcomes in a highly regulated environment.

This position is ideal for a project management professional with extensive experience in **hydroelectric facilities, dam maintenance and rehabilitation, marine construction, power generation, or other complex infrastructure projects** requiring regulatory oversight and stakeholder coordination.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Project Leadership & Delivery:**

* Lead large, complex hydroelectric dam maintenance and infrastructure projects through all phases of the project lifecycle, including initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closeout.
* Deliver projects on scope, schedule, budget, quality, and risk objectives using established project management methodologies and best practices.
* Define project requirements, business objectives, deliverables, and technical specifications while developing comprehensive project execution plans.
* Build and manage project teams by aligning resources, expertise, and organizational capabilities with project complexity and risk.

**Contract & Construction Management:**

* Manage project contracts and vendor relationships in partnership with procurement and sourcing teams.
* Oversee contractor performance, compliance, and commercial execution to ensure successful delivery.
* Ensure all work is completed safely, meets technical specifications, and adheres to contractual commitments and project schedules.
* Coordinate construction, maintenance, engineering, and operational activities throughout project execution.

**Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management:**

* Ensure projects comply with applicable regulatory requirements, including Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) standards and related industry regulations.
* Maintain complete and accurate project documentation, records, permits, and compliance files.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate project risks while implementing effective risk management strategies.
* Support regulatory reviews, audits, reporting requirements, and stakeholder communications.

**Stakeholder Engagement & Communication:**

* Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders.
* Provide clear and timely communication regarding project status, risks, milestones, decisions, and performance.
* Coordinate effectively with engineering teams, operations personnel, contractors, consultants, regulatory agencies, and executive leadership.
* Foster strong working relationships and facilitate collaboration across multiple business units and project stakeholders.

**Project Controls & Closeout:**

* Establish project performance metrics, reporting processes, and governance practices.
* Conduct project feasibility assessments, cost-benefit analyses, and business case evaluations.
* Lead project closeout activities, including operational turnover, financial reconciliation, documentation completion, and resource transitions.
* Support organizational project management initiatives and mentor team members in project delivery and change management practices.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Project Management Professional (**PMP**) certification.
* Minimum of **9 years of experience** leading large, complex infrastructure, construction, maintenance, engineering, or energy-related projects.
* Proven experience managing projects in regulated environments.
* Experience with dam maintenance, heavy civil construction, marine construction, hydroelectric facilities, power generation, or similar critical infrastructure projects.
* Demonstrated success managing project scope, budgets, schedules, contracts, and risks.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Civil, Structural, or Mechanical Engineering.
* Professional Engineer (**PE**) licensure, preferably in Wisconsin.
* Dam Safety Engineer (**DSE**) background or related dam safety experience.
* Experience working with FERC regulations and hydroelectric infrastructure.
* Knowledge of utility, energy generation, or large-scale public infrastructure projects.

description:
**Assistant Project Manager**

Uncommon Developers is a fast-growing company that strives to re-imagine what a community can be and how it’s built. We are committed in being innovating, leading edge technology & excellent customer service. Our onsite employees are outgoing, caring and proud of whom they represent. If you are looking to be a part of our fast-growing company & looking for a professional rewarding career, we look forward to hearing from you.

**Description**

The Assistant Project Manager is to play a pivotal role in supporting the Senior Project Manager (or Project Manager) and Superintendent in all facets of project execution. This position acts as a liaison among the architect, engineer, and subcontractors.

**What You'll Be Doing:**

\\*

Coordinate with architect and provide ideas for construction procedures and details

* Analyze drawings, specifications, proposals, and project site evaluation to assist Project Manager in developing schedules and tracking project costs

* Work with architects and provide ideas for construction and design during the project pre-development stage

* Process administrative work including subcontractor bidding process, project cost updates, and constructability review of documents

* Resolve field issues as they arise

* Assist the Project Managers in the following activities:

Job start-up including special procurements and long lead time items

* Project Buyout (i.e., bidding process, bid comparisons, negotiations of contracts, purchase orders)

* Draft change orders to contracts and purchase orders

* Prepare G-702 Draw, Payment Request to Lender

* Invoice approval process with ongoing projects

* Track the due diligence process and scheduling for projects under pre-development, as needed

* Provide input in the budgeting process for projects in pre-development, as needed. This will encompass both predevelopment and construction budgets.

* Develop subcontracts and procure permits.

* Solve problems and trouble-shoot in conjunction with the assigned project

* Review system function and operation with subcontractors

* Give any suggestions to your project managers, area managers and/or division Vice President which may provide a more efficient way to work

* Resolve RFI’s, and maintain and update RFI Log

* Review submittals in conjunction with project management and maintain and update submission log

* Ensure all documentation procedures are being followed (e.g., as-builts, permit books, warranty books, insurance certificates, etc.)

* Ensure all invoices and change orders are reviewed in a timely manner

* Maintain and update as-built; document log, and provide the field with the latest set of documents (field, consultants and contractors)

* Compile lender inspection information

* Compile information to use in scope of contract

* Update Sheet Index for contract documents

* Maintain and update inspection reports

* Maintain and update transmittal and tracking logs

* Set up and maintain job files

* Attend work as scheduled to support the ongoing success of the company

* Other duties as assigned by manager

**Skill We're Seeking:**

You’ve mastered Project Controls including RFI, the submission process, change tracking, ASI’s and more. You’re a pro at communicating on and off the page. On top of that, you’re fluent in interpreting and understanding plans and specifications. And you’re able to do all of that because you’re organized and can manage multiple tasks and projects simultaneously.

* Degree in construction management or civil engineering
* Project experience on jobs in excess of $15 million each
* Minimum 2 years work history in related field/position
* Proficiency in Excel, Word, MS Project/Primavera, and Prolog/Constructware, Procore (or equivalent)
* Commercial and/or multifamily experience required

**Salary: Competitive with benefits DOE.**

**\\*Must be able to successfully pass a background and drug screen.**

We are an equal opportunity employer. Uncommon Developers does not discriminate against any applicant or employee based on race, religion, color, creed, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, marital status, pregnancy, medical condition, disability, military status, sexual orientation, or any other consideration which violates federal, state or local laws.

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $90,000.00 - $116,000.00 per year

description:
CampusWorks is seeking an Infrastructure Administrator to provide hands-on administration and operational support for client datacenter, server, cloud-connected, security, and network infrastructure.

The primary focus of this position is the administration, maintenance, monitoring, and operational stability of enterprise systems and datacenter technologies, including Microsoft server environments, identity and access services, virtualization platforms, infrastructure monitoring, security controls, and related technologies. The position also supports campus networking infrastructure as operational needs arise.

The Infrastructure Administrator formally reports to the Associate CIO and operates as a member of the institution's infrastructure team. Day-to-day technical direction, infrastructure priorities, work assignments, project delegation, technical review, and operational coordination are led by the Senior Infrastructure Engineer, who serves as the primary technical lead for systems, networking, security, and datacenter infrastructure.

The position works closely with the Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Network Engineer, Associate CIO, institutional technology leadership, CampusWorks Centers of Excellence (CoEs), other IT teams, and external vendors to maintain reliable, secure, and supportable technology services and advance infrastructure modernization initiatives.

### **Essential Job Duties:**

* Install, configure, administer, maintain, patch, and upgrade Microsoft Windows Server and related enterprise infrastructure technologies.

* Support core infrastructure and identity services including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, certificate services, file services, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Azure-connected services, and hybrid identity technologies.

* Administer and support enterprise virtualization platforms and associated server infrastructure, including provisioning, configuration, monitoring, troubleshooting, performance, and lifecycle management.

description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

The Sr. Principal Engineer, Project Planning & Scheduling serves as GFD's enterprise process owner for planning and scheduling across the global capital portfolio. * Define and govern schedule quality requirements, including schedule development, logic integrity, critical path methodology, progress measurement, forecasting, schedule risk analysis, and schedule performance management.
* Lead planning and scheduling assurance activities across the portfolio to verify compliance with enterprise standards and drive corrective actions where deficiencies are identified.
* Establish planning and scheduling requirements for contractors, consultants, and delivery partners and ensure consistent implementation across projects and regions.
* Serve as GFD's senior technical SME for schedule recovery, acceleration planning, scenario analysis, forecasting, and schedule risk mitigation.
* Govern enterprise KPIs and performance measures related to schedule quality, forecasting accuracy, schedule predictability, and project delivery performance.
* Partner with project teams, contractors, and business partners to improve scheduling capability, strengthen project execution strategies, and promote adoption of best practices.
* Build organizational capability through training, mentoring, communities of practice, and continuous improvement initiatives that advance planning and scheduling excellence across the portfolio.

Minimum Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Business, Supply Chain, or a related discipline, or equivalent work experience.
* Demonstrated expertise in planning and scheduling for large, complex capital projects, including development, governance, and assurance of integrated schedules, application of critical path methodology, forecasting, schedule risk analysis, and establishment of enterprise scheduling standards and best practices.
* Proficiency with Primavera P6
* Ability and willingness to travel up to 25%.
* Position is based in Indianapolis, Indiana.
* Qualified applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Lilly will not provide support for or sponsor work authorization or visas for this role, including but not limited to F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, J-1, H-1B, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, or L-1.

* Professional certification from AACE International, PMI, CMAA, or a similar professional organization.
* Experience serving as a planning and scheduling lead, center-of-excellence lead, or process owner supporting large capital project portfolios.
* Experience supporting integrated project delivery across engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, qualification and validation (CQV), startup, operational readiness, and operational handover.
* Experience supporting pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, or other complex industrial capital programs, including contractor scheduling governance and assurance.
* Proficiency with enterprise planning, scheduling, project controls, and project information management systems, including application of integrated maste

description:
The Senior Project Executive is a senior leader responsible for overseeing the successful delivery of public-sector design-build projects in New York City. This role provides strategic leadership across project execution, client relations, contract negotiations, financial oversight, and business development. The Senior Project Executive serves as the primary client-facing leader, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in full compliance with NYC procurement and MWBE and diversity requirements.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Leadership & Oversight:** Provide executive-level direction across multiple high-value design-build projects, ensuring alignment with firm objectives, client goals, and public-sector compliance requirements.
* **Client Relations:** Act as the primary point of contact for senior client representatives, fostering strong relationships and ensuring client satisfaction throughout project lifecycles.
* **Financial Management:** Oversee budgets, forecasts, and profitability for assigned projects; lead margin optimization, risk analysis, and financial reporting in collaboration with project controls.
* **Contract & Risk Management:** Negotiate, review, and manage contracts with owners, consultants, and subcontractors; ensure compliance with AIA contract documents, NYC public procurement regulations, and MWBE goals.
* **Business Development:** Partner with executive leadership to identify and pursue new public-sector opportunities, leveraging client relationships to support growth.
* **Operational Excellence:** Drive project team performance, ensuring adherence to schedule, safety standards, quality metrics, and regulatory requirements.
* **Mentorship:** Provide guidance and leadership to Project Managers and other senior staff, supporting talent development and succession planning within the firm.

**Required Qualifications**

* 15+ years of progressive experience in construction management, with at least 5 years in an executive or senior leadership role.
* Experience delivering high value design-build projects, projects delivered for government entities are preferred.
* Proven track record delivering public-sector projects in NYC (DDC, SCA, NYCHA, DEP, or similar agencies).
* Strong knowledge of NYC procurement processes, MWBE and diversity compliance, prevailing wage, and public contract requirements.
* Demonstrated success in client-facing leadership roles with the ability to develop long-term relationships.
* Expertise in financial oversight, including P&L responsibility, budgeting, forecasting, and margin management.
* Proficiency in construction management software: Procore, CMiC, Textura, or similar platforms.
* Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or related field.
* DBIA or Associate DBIA certification.

**Preferred Attributes**

* Strong business development acumen with established relationships in NYC’s public-sector market.
* Exceptional communication, negotiation, and leadership skills.
* Ability to drive innovation in project delivery while ensuring compliance and profitability.

**What We Offer**

* Safe Harbor 401(k) Plan
* Health, Dental and Vision insurance
* Company-paid disability and life insurance
* Voluntary life insurance
* Paid time off & sick time
* Pre-Tax Commuter Benefits
* Health & Wellness Reimbursements
* Opportunities for professional development and career advancement
* A collaborative and dynamic work environment

*Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.*

SLSCO LTD is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without discrimination because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other federal, state, or local protected class.

SLSCO strongly encourages New York City Housing Authority residents to submit their application and resume for this job opportunity.

**Service Forester, Natural Resource Specialist 2 (NRS2)**
**Recruitment #2026-10-7410**
**Full-time, Non-permanent, Represented position (WPEA)**
**Anticipated Non-permanent end date is June 30, 2027**
**Location: Northeast Region - Deer Park, WA**

**Work Hour flexibility may be available and considered**
**Salary: $4,517.00 - $6,075.00 Monthly**

**Review of applications is ongoing.** We reserve the right to make a hiring decision or close this recruitment at any time after 10/15/2026. It is in your best interest to submit materials as soon as possible.

**Want to join something GREAT and make a difference?**

The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Northeast Region is looking to fill a **Service Forester (NRS2)** position based out of our Deer Park location, helping provide coverage in both Spokane and Stevens County. We are looking for an individual who is a proven team player, has experience in forestry, forest health, and fire suppression, and displays an effective form of leadership to deliver program goals to local landowners.

The local work unit is dominated by pine stands in desperate need of treatments to promote forest health, reduce fuel loading, and protect structures. Since 2020, hundreds of people have purchased open lands within the work unit in hopes of building their dream houses, and oftentimes these places are overrun with pine thickets and overcrowded forests in poor health. This position will help to support the private landowners in protecting their dream and the surrounding communities. Thousands of existing homes and properties are losing the battle every year trying to manage the forest that never stops growing. The Service Forester’s decisions on timber and biomass management are very important and can certainly put a property on a better trajectory of good forest health, which is a cornerstone goal of the program.

The Service Forester position will report to the Sr. Service Forester (NRS3) and will require the ability to foster positive working relationships amongst the other Service Foresters in the county and region, while also interacting with the general public, contractors, fire districts, and other state, local, county, and federal agencies on a routine basis. This position will require the successful candidate to exercise their knowledge of forestry, forest health, fire behavior, structural protection, agreement negotiation, and communication skills. By performing these actions effectively, efficiently, and professionally, the Service Forester supports the DNR in fulfilling its mission of providing innovative leadership and expertise to ensure environmental protection, community safety, and a rich quality of life for current and future generations.

**Duties**
----------

**Responsibilities:**

* Under the direction of the Senior Service Forester, provide on-site or remote professional guidance and technical expertise to forest landowners (and forest landowner service providers) regarding forest management and structure risk reduction.
* Assist with facilitating landowner participation in financial assistance programs and forest health or fuel reduction contracts.
* Collaborate with other agency partners to help customize a plan of action for the landowner.
* Serve as a technical and professional resource for educational programs.
* On assigned projects, design work units on the ground for the purpose of utilizing funds within the cost share program.
* Complete home risk assessments.
* Enter and provide documentation for all inquiries and services provided into the One Stop Shop Online Tracking Tool.

**Qualifications**
------------------

**Required Qualifications:**

*You must meet all the Required Qualifications and Competencies to be considered for this position. There are multiple pathways to meet qualifications, such as education, volunteer work, life skills, and experience. Please clearly communicate in your application material that your skills align with the position and qualifications.*

* Bachelor of Science in forestry, natural resources, or closely related field from an accredited program;

AND one year of field experience in forest management;

OR an equivalent combination of education, training, and professional experience that demonstrates the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.
* Experience in general forest management activities such as forest road design and construction, timber management planning, silviculture techniques, reforestation methods, and timber harvest boundaries.
* Experience using forestry tools such as measuring and hand tools.
* Proficient with computers, Microsoft Office applications, and SharePoint.
* Experience with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), including ArcPro, ArcGIS Online, Survey123, Field Maps, or other mapping tools to document work and convey information to non-technical audiences.

**Required Competencies:**

* Takes initiative

Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programs as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include program, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier program, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

**Job Description**

**Turner & Townsend** is seeking an experienced **Senior Scheduler** to join our team to support scheduling as a project controls function on a large-scale project. The ideal individual will have a proven track record of successfully delivering construction project control services.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop, monitor and update owners' Project Integrated Master Schedule (IMS).
* Establish the schedule management program and deliverables to be used on large scale capital programs.
* Interface with project stakeholders as trusted advisors to provide guidance and recommendations for the project.
* Prepare baseline schedules and schedule basis documents for approval by project teams.
* Conduct schedule of resource loading and leveling.
* Consolidate contractors schedule to incorporate into IMS.
* Assess impacts on the critical path and near-critical activities and report to the project team.
* Monitor schedule deviations and variances and assist in the development of alternative methods for corrective action.
* Apply EVM methodology to measure project progress.
* Review schedules with project team members on a regular basis to ensure that accurate and timely data is incorporated into the schedule.
* Prepare and provide schedule progress reports, trending charts, and schedule analysis on a periodic basis.
* Maintain record of scope changes, trends and variances that potentially affect schedule performance.
* Assure the credibility of the information contained in the schedule.
* Maintain liaison with clients and other consultants at all projects stages.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in construction management, cost management, quantity surveying, engineering or field related to construction.
* Minimum 5-7 years of applicable experience.
* Direct experience working on teams within a complex matrix environment.
* Expertise using Primavera P6.
* Excellent communication skills.

**Additional Information**

**\\*On site requirements might change based on client needs\\***

*SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.*

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change. We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

Turner & Townsend is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and actively encourage applications from all sectors of the community.

Turner & Townsend does not accept any speculative or unsolicited CV’s that have been sent to our internal recruitment team or hiring managers from agencies outside of our preferred supplier list. Any speculative or unsolicited CV’s will be treated as a direct application.

It is strictly against Turner & Townsend policy for candidates to pay any fee in relation to our recruitment process. No recruitment agency working with Turner & Townsend will ask candidates to pay a fee at any time.

description:
The Durham Housing Authority is seeking an experienced and driven Capital Fund Project Manager to lead transformative capital improvement and development initiatives that directly impact the quality of housing and services provided to our residents.

This is an exciting and highly collaborative opportunity for a project management professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys leading complex construction and redevelopment projects, and wants to make a lasting difference in the community. ====================

The Capital Fund Project Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating, and overseeing capital improvement projects from concept through completion. This position provides leadership in project planning, budgeting, procurement, construction oversight, regulatory compliance, stakeholder engagement, and risk management.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Real Estate Development, the successful candidate will work closely with contractors, architects, engineers, public officials, residents, and agency leadership to ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in compliance with all applicable requirements.

--------------------

* Coordinate the implementation of capital improvement projects for Public Housing, RAD, and development initiatives.
* Manage project schedules, budgets, and expenditures.
* Oversee project planning, design, procurement, construction, and closeout activities.
* Serve as the primary liaison with architects, engineers, contractors, consultants, and regulatory agencies.
* Develop and administer RFP and bid solicitation processes.
* Ensure compliance with HUD requirements, local codes, regulations, and contractual obligations.
* Monitor project performance and provide detailed reports to senior leadership.
* Identify project risks and develop mitigation strategies.
* Track milestones, deliverables, budgets, and action items.
* Conduct stakeholder meetings and presentations, including engagement with residents, boards, and community groups.
* Lead project teams and foster collaboration among internal and external stakeholders.
* Continually identify opportunities to improve project delivery processes and maximize capital investments.
* Support funding, investment, and development initiatives as assigned.
* Collaborates with Operations and Maintenance leadership to plan, coordinate, and execute key Capital Fund Program projects and initiatives.

**Education Required**

* Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Project Management, Urban Planning, Real Estate Development, or a closely related field.

**Experience Required**

* Significant experience managing construction, capital improvement, redevelopment, or infrastructure projects.
* Experience administering procurement processes, construction contracts, budgets, and project schedules.
* Experience overseeing compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
* Experience managing multiple complex projects simultaneously.

**Preferred Education**

* Master's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Public Administration, Business Administration, Real Estate Development, or a related field.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience working with Public Housing Authorities, affordable housing organizations, or government-funded development projects.
* Experience with HUD Capital Fund, RAD, LIHTC, or other affordable housing development programs.
* Experience presenting to executive leadership, governing boards, and public stakeholders.
* Experience leading large-scale redevelopment or modernization projects.

-----------------------

**Project Leadership**

* Ability to lead complex projects from planning through completion.
* Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Ability to manage competing priorities while meeting deadlines.

* Knowledge of residential and commercial construction practices.
* Ability to interpret plans, specifications, contracts, and construction documents.
* Knowledge of project budgeting, scheduling, procurement, and contract administration.

* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to build productive relationships with contractors, consultants, residents, government officials, and agency leadership.
* Ability to facilitate meetings and make professional presentations.

* Ability to identify risks, develop solutions, and drive projects to successful completion.

**Make an impact at NTT Global Data Centers**

Join NTT Global Data Centers and be part of a team that drives innovation and sustainability in the digital world. With over 150 data centers across more than 20 countries globally, we offer unparalleled opportunities to work on cutting-edge technology and transformative projects. Experience a collaborative, innovative, and inclusive workplace where your ideas are valued, and your growth is supported.

**Your role at a glance**

The Director, Engineering Standards and Safety is a global role, that leads the global function that defines how engineering work is performed safely and consistently across data center operations. The role owns engineering standards, technical methods, operating boundaries, asset-acceptance criteria and the governance of technical deviations and risk acceptances. This director leads a multidisciplinary team covering electrical, mechanical, controls, fire and life safety, and related engineering disciplines. The discipline standards engineers carry the primary research, evidence development, consultation and drafting workload. The Director sets priorities, challenges the evidence and retains final approval and governance authority. The function works with Field Engineering, Operations, Design, Construction, Commissioning, vendors and corporate safety teams to convert technical risk and operating experience into practical global requirements. Regional teams remain accountable for executing engineering work. Clear standards and safety controls help operating teams run critical facilities safely and efficiently, maintain reliable infrastructure, reduce avoidable environmental impact and provide consistent technical support to clients.

**What we are looking for**

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Set the global strategy, priorities and operating model for Engineering Standards & Safety.
* Set the standards-development portfolio and research priorities, assign accountable discipline engineers and ensure work is proportionate to risk and business need.
* Review and approve engineering standards, technical methods and analytical models developed through documented research and cross-functional consultation.
* Ensure discipline engineers engage Field Engineering, site Operations, vendors and other experts, reconcile material input and maintain a traceable technical basis for each recommendation.
* Define technical operating limits, system boundaries and escalation requirements for electrical, mechanical, controls, fire and life-safety systems.
* Establish engineering acceptance criteria for assets and systems entering operation, in partnership with Design, Construction, Commissioning and Operations.
* Define validation frameworks for reliability analysis, energy analysis, technical-capacity analysis and control-strategy design.
* Own the governance process for technical deviations and engineering risk acceptances, including approval authorities, evidence requirements, review periods and escalation thresholds.
* Define engineering safety requirements for energized work, arc-flash risk, breaker coordination and other high-risk engineering activities.
* Establish global control-system and alarm philosophy, including control-sequence principles, setpoint governance, alarm requirements, point naming, tagging and metadata standards.
* Establish fire and life-safety engineering requirements and assurance methods in partnership with corporate safety, regional teams and authorities having jurisdiction.
* Monitor adoption of standards, identify systemic compliance gaps and sponsor corrective actions without assuming regional execution ownership.
* Ensure standards reflect operating experience, incident learning, regulatory requirements, recognized industry practices and changes in technology.
* Chair or sponsor governance forums that resolve cross-region technical questions, approve material exceptions and assign clear decision ownership.
* Build and lead a high-performing global team through workforce planning, hiring, coaching, performance management and succession planning.
* Communicate engineering requirements, material risks and decisions to senior leaders in clear technical and business terms.
Manage the function's priorities, resources, external technical support and budget in line with approved business plans.

**ROLE AND DECISION SCOPEKE**

**Owns**

* Global engineering standards, methods and technical governance for operating facilities.
* Technical operating boundaries and asset-acceptance criteria.
* Engineering-safety requirements within the function's remit.
* Control and alarm philosophy and related naming, tagging and metadata standards.
* The engineering deviation and risk-acceptance framework.
* Assurance methods for adoption and continued suitability of standards.

**Approves**

* New and materially revised global engineering standards.
* Standards-development priorities and the evidence required before a proposal enters formal app

About Bee Green Recycling & Supply

Bee Green is a purpose-driven company serving the Bay Area through our Recycling Services, Landscape Supply Yard, and Power Equipment Dealership. **We’re a hive of activity—with people at the center of everything we do!** Our mission is simple: **Helping You Succeed... Professionally. Personally. Spiritually.** We believe every person is made in the image of God and deserves to be treated with dignity, worth, and purpose. That belief drives how we serve, support, and protect our customers, coworkers, vendors, and community. It's also why we build our team around these core values:

**Live with Integrity -** We are people of our word. We do the right thing even when no one is watching.

**Provide Excellent Service** – We serve others with genuine care, excellence, and a heart to help.

**Strive for Continual Improvement** – We stay teachable and open to feedback, always looking for ways to grow.

**Work Safely** – We protect ourselves and others by prioritizing safety in every task.

**Steward All Resources & Abilities Well** – We manage what we've been given with purpose and responsibility.

The Position

The **Head of Purchasing & Receiving** is responsible for ordering all inventory, for sourcing and ordering products, maintaining optimal inventory levels, and ensuring that all received goods are accurately accounted for and properly recorded. The Head of Purchasing & Receiving must have a keen eye for accuracy, budget management, and supply chain logistics. The Head of Purchasing & Receiving reports to the Inventory Manager.

### **Our Benefits**

* Medical Insurance

* Dental, Vision, Supplemental, and Life Insurance
* PTO
* 401(k) with 5% Company Contribution

* Right Now Media At Work (Personal & Professional Development Video Library)
* SmartDollar Financial Wellness Tools (Including free access to financial coaches!)
* Chaplaincy Care

### **What You'd Be Doing**

* Maintain optimal stock levels by analyzing sales trends, seasonal demand, and historical usage.
* Work closely with Yard Supervisors, Lead CSR, Turf & Hardscape Lead, Stocking & Facing Clerks, and Inventory Manager to establish upcoming inventory needs.
* Generate and manage purchase orders (POs) based on store needs, supplier lead times, and budget constraints, and send to Logistics Coordinator for scheduling transportation.
* Monitor and manage inventory turnover, ensuring efficient purchasing to avoid stock shortages or overages.
* Monitor designated purchasing budget and ensure that all purchases fall within the established budgetary constraints.
* Oversee all incoming shipments, ensuring proper handling and verification as soon as product is received on site.
* Supervise the receiving team to ensure inventory is accurately counted, inspected for quality, and properly recorded in the system.
* Address and resolve discrepancies such as short shipments, damaged goods, or incorrect deliveries with suppliers.
* Maintain detailed and accurate records of all purchases, shipments, and inventory adjustments.
* Assist in periodic inventory audits and cycle counts to maintain accurate records.
* Monitor purchase orders still open past expiration date and follow up with vendors on order status.

### **Requirements**

* At least 18 years old and legally eligible to work in the U.S.
* Proficient in Epicor Biztrack, and Microsoft office suite (especially in Word and Excel).
* Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
* Excellent written and verbal communication
* Ability to lift and handle products up to 50 lbs and work with materials of varied shapes and sizes
* Team-oriented mindset and a proactive, problem-solving approach
* Alignment with company Mission & Core Values, and passionate interest in partnering with Bee Green to pursue said mission & core values.

### **Experience Needed (One of the Following)**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Logistics, or related field.
* Certification in logistics or supply chain and minimum of 1-2 years of recent experience in logistics, shipping/receiving, or supply chain management, or related role.
* 4 years of recent experience in logistics, shipping/receiving, or supply chain management, or related role.

Range Dependent on skills and experience

**THIS IS A DRUG FREE WORKPLACE**

*This organization does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, sex (includes pregnancy, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation), disability (mental and physical), medical condition, age (40 or older), genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, or on the basis of any other legally protected reason.*

**Company Overview**

Holafly is a high-growth scale-up revolutionising how businesses and travellers connect to the internet abroad. Since 2018, we’ve empowered travellers in over 200 destinations worldwide with secure and reliable eSIM solutions. With a team of 800+ professionals across multiple countries, we are scaling globally to support travellers with seamless, unlimited data connectivity.

We’re not just connecting people—we’re enabling freedom and peace of mind, ensuring our users stay connected from the second they land, wherever their journey takes them.

**The Role**

As our first Head of Procurement, you will build our global procurement function from scratch, directly driving profitability through strategic vendor alignment. Your leadership will secure critical telecom partnerships and transform procurement into a sustainable growth engine.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Build Holafly's global procurement strategy from the ground up to support rapid international expansion.
* Negotiate high-stakes telecom contracts to secure top-tier pricing, quality, and SLA terms across markets.
* Establish company-wide procurement policies and vendor risk frameworks for governance.
* Optimize global supplier spend, unlocking cost savings without compromising service quality.
* Scale vendor performance metrics to ensure long-term supplier reliability across 200+ destinations.
* Partner with cross-functional leadership to align procurement goals with overarching product strategy.

**Qualifications**

* Proven procurement leadership, +5 years exp. ideally within a fast-growing scale-up or tech environment.
* Direct experience building procurement frameworks and vendor management workflows from zero.
* Expertise in international contract negotiations and financial analysis for complex service agreements.
* Strong leadership capabilities with a passion for designing scalable processes.

**Nice to Have**

* Background in Telecom, Connectivity, or SaaS environments.
* Knowledge of international vendor compliance and cross-border operations.

**Benefits & Perks**

* Fully Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with trust-based flexibility and a focus on work-life balance.
* Professional Development Stipend: Dedicated budgets for continuous education, courses, and certifications.
* Global Scale-Up Impact: Direct influence on the future of connectivity within an international culture.
* Competitive Package: Enjoy comprehensive benefits, continuous learning, and real opportunities for career growth.

description:
**Summary:**

* The Chief Procurement Officer has oversight for the procurement program for all County offices, including developing and implementing procurement policies and procedures and oversees the professional and clerical staff.

**Essential Duties:**

* Manage the County's centralized purchasing function including the procurement activities of the professional and clerical staff.
* Establish departmental objectives, directs priorities, interprets purchasing policies, rules, and regulations governing procurement activities.
* Maintain relationships with contractors and suppliers to resolve problems, explore new business opportunities and maintain productive partnerships.
* Assist and educate County personnel of all levels in resolving purchasing discrepancies and familiarizing managers with purchasing laws in areas from processing requisitions to conforming to terms and conditions of contracts.
* Develop specifications and documents for solicitation of public Invitations to Bid and Requests for Proposals on major procurements of equipment, materials and services for all County agencies.
* Oversee conduct of the bidding process, insuring compliance with legal, regulatory and other requirements governing public procurement.
* Interview and work with contractors, suppliers, department heads and other officials concerning the purchasing of supplies and equipment.
* Function as chairperson of RFP evaluation committees (when applicable); provides technical expertise concerning contract specifications; analyzes bid and proposal responses, and administers the entire formal public bidding process.
* Participate in professional or collegial organizations that provide information and/or purchasing opportunities for the County, e.g. Lehigh Valley Cooperative Purchasing Council (LVCPC), the Southeastern Pennsylvania Counties Cooperative Purchasing Board (SPCCPB), the Pennsylvania Public Purchasing Association (PAPPA), NIGP: The Institute for Public Procurement.
* Perform related work as needed.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* The Chief Procurement Officer has supervisory responsibility for approximately (6) direct reports.

**Qualifications:**

* To perform this job successfully, the individual in this position must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the minimum knowledge, skills and ability required.

**Education/Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree (B. A.) from four-year college or university; or one to two years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Minimum of five (5) years' experience procuring goods and services, and managing competitive bids/proposals with the responsibility of at least $10 million in purchases annually and at least 30 user departments. Public procurement experience preferred, including familiarity with all aspects of Invitations to Bid and Requests for Proposal.
* Thorough knowledge of goals, objectives, methods and techniques applicable to the management of a centralized procurement program.
* Extensive knowledge and understanding of County policies and procedures, general law of contracts and Commonwealth, Federal, cooperative and other types of contracts.
* Thorough knowledge of methods, techniques and legal requirements commonly employed in purchasing commodities and services used by government at the local level.
* Thorough knowledge in using personal computers including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and Outlook) and internet applications.

description:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.

**About the Role**
==================

Square is looking for a senior operations leader to define and manage the global external workforce and partner strategy for seller onboarding. Reporting to the Head of Global Onboarding Operations, this leader will own the operating model for third-party service providers, vendors, and BPO partners, ensuring that external delivery capacity improves seller outcomes while scaling efficiently and responsibly.

This role sits at the intersection of operations, workforce strategy, vendor governance, finance, procurement, legal, and regional execution. The right candidate can evaluate complex build-vs-buy tradeoffs, establish global partner standards, influence senior stakeholders, and create governance mechanisms that improve quality, cost, consistency, and scalability across markets.

**What You Will Own**
=====================

**External Workforce Strategy**
-------------------------------

* Develop and maintain the global strategy for vendors, third-party service providers, and BPO partners supporting seller onboarding.
* Partner with regional operations leaders to determine the right labor mix by market, seller segment, service tier, and business need.
* Lead build-vs-buy analyses and recommend when work should be handled by first-party teams, vendors, BPO, partners, or self-serve models.
* Create scalable frameworks for external workforce footprint, capacity, quality, cost, and market coverage.

**Partner Governance and Performance**
--------------------------------------

* Establish global SLA frameworks, scorecards, quality standards, business review cadences, and escalation mechanisms for external partners.
* Hold vendors and BPO partners accountable for operational performance, seller experience, compliance with standards, and continuous improvement.
* Partner with Procurement, Legal, Finance, and regional teams on contracts, renewals, pricing structures, and commercial terms.

**BPO and Vendor Operating Model**
----------------------------------

* Oversee the operating model for BPO and vendor-supported onboarding work, including role clarity, performance expectations, enablement, quality assurance, and escalation paths.
* Ensure partner operations are integrated with Square’s broader onboarding workflows, data, tooling, and seller experience standards.
* Identify opportunities to improve partner productivity, reduce cost-to-serve, and increase consistency across geographies.

**Cross-Functional Leadership**
-------------------------------

* Influence senior leaders across Sales, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and regional teams.
* Translate external workforce performance and market needs into strategic recommendations for investment, partner selection, and operating model changes.
* Navigate sensitive partner and stakeholder situations while maintaining strong internal and external relationships.

**Team Leadership**
-------------------

* Manage partner operations managers, BPO leaders, vendor managers, or related teams as the organization evolves.
* Develop leaders and build a culture of accountability, commercial rigor, operational discipline, and seller-focused execution.

**What We Are Looking For**
===========================

* 12+ years of progressive operations, vendor management, partner operations, BPO, procurement-adjacent, or workforce strategy experience.
* Deep experience managing third-party providers, BPOs, vendors, or outsourced service delivery at scale.
* Strong understanding of SLAs, partner governance, quality assurance, operational scorecards, and business review mechanisms.

The Kentucky Department of Corrections (DOC), Division of Adult Institutions operates 13 correctional facilities that house Kentucky's adult inmate population. The mission of DOC is to protect the citizens of the Commonwealth and to provide a safe, secure and humane environment for staff and offenders in carrying out the mandates of the legislative and judicial processes; and, to provide opportunities for offenders to acquire skills which facilitate non-criminal behavior.

This position is for the new Medical Facility, located on the grounds of Blackburn Correctional Complex.

If you are looking for a career within the Department of Corrections that provides opportunity for career development, then the Department of Corrections may have an opportunity for you! We are hiring a Purchasing Officer I. This position performs beginning level duties in the procurement of and, or, payment of goods and non-professional services on an agency wide-basis.

Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

* Gathers, prepares and maintains purchase and payment documents.
* Works with vendors to collect quotes, invoices and etc.
* Pro Card Holder and reconciles purchases.
* Monitors purchases made for conformance with the Model Procurement Code, (KRS 45A)
* Performs beginning level duties in the performance of and, or, payment of goods and non-professional services in accordance with the agency’s Small Purchase Authority.
* Performs other duties as directed by Fiscal Manager and Supervisor.

Minimum Requirements

**EDUCATION:** Graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree.

**EXPERIENCE, TRAINING, OR SKILLS:** NONE

**Substitute EDUCATION for EXPERIENCE:** NONE

**Substitute EXPERIENCE for EDUCATION:** Experience in purchasing will substitute for the required college on a year for year basis. Certification with the National Institute of Governmental Purchasing as a Certified Professional Public Buyer (CPPB) will substitute for one year of the college requirement OR certification as a Certified Public Purchasing Officer (CPPO) will substitute for two years of the college requirement.

**SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS (AGE, LICENSURE, REGULATION, ETC.):** NONE

Working Conditions

Incumbents working in this job title perform duties in an office setting.

Probationary Period

This job has an initial and promotional probationary period of 6 months, except as provided in KRS 18A.111.

If you have questions about this advertisement, please contact Kasey Schank at Kasey.Schank@ky.gov

The Procurement and Asset Management Officer provides organization-wide leadership for procurement, purchasing systems, vendor and contract management, inventory control, and fixed-asset administration. The position establishes and maintains procurement policies, approval workflows, vendor standards, reporting requirements, and system controls designed to promote cost efficiency, accountability, compliance, and operational reliability.

The position has primary responsibility for administering and continuously improving the organization’s procurement and purchase-order systems and works closely with executive leadership, Finance, Accounts Payable, Information Technology, Facilities, and department heads.

The Officer exercises organization-wide functional authority over procurement and asset-management processes within delegated limits established by the Executive Director and the organization’s Procurement Policy. The position supports compliance with the Board-approved budget but does not independently approve organizational budgets, transfer funds, authorize unbudgeted expenditures, or execute contracts unless specifically delegated by the Executive Director. Department heads remain responsible for departmental operations and budgets, subject to executive oversight. This authority is exercised under the direction and oversight of the COO and does not supersede the authority of the Executive Director, CFO, executive team, or Board of Directors

Procurement and Strategic Sourcing

* Lead and administer centralized procurement across all departments.
* Develop, recommend, and enforce purchasing policies within delegated authority.
* Review purchasing requests for compliance with policy, budget, specifications, and documentation requirements.
* Manage sourcing, bidding, vendor selection, contract negotiations, renewals, and supplier performance within delegated authority.
* Identify cost savings, cost avoidance, volume discounts, standardization opportunities, and purchasing efficiencies.
* Monitor spending by department, category, vendor, contract, and budget.
* Address noncompliant, emergency, duplicate, unauthorized, and off-contract purchases.

Procurement Systems and Process Improvement

* Administer and continuously improve the organization’s procurement and purchase-order systems, including workflow design, user access, system configuration, data integrity, reporting, documentation, training, procure-to-pay procedures, and coordination with Finance, Accounts Payable, Information Technology, and department users.

* Establish performance measures and continuously improve procurement processes and service delivery.
* Establish inventory standards, item classifications, reorder points, safety-stock levels, cycle counts, and stockroom procedures.
* Maintain accurate inventory records and investigate variances, shortages, excess stock, obsolete materials, and receiving discrepancies.
* Implement barcode or QR-code tracking where appropriate.
* Optimize purchasing schedules, order consolidation, product standardization, and inventory levels.

Fixed-Asset Management

* Maintain accurate records of assets from acquisition through assignment, transfer, maintenance, retirement, and disposal.
* Track equipment, technology, facilities assets, furnishings, and other organizational properties,
* Maintain information regarding asset location, custodian, condition, serial number, warranty, service history, and replacement needs.
* Coordinate asset inventories, reconciliations, transfers, secure disposal, and retirement with Finance, Information Technology, Facilities, and other departments.
* Support lifecycle planning, warranty management, preventive maintenance, and capital-replacement forecasting.

Executive Reporting and Planning

* Provide reports to the COO, CFO, and executive leadership regarding expenditures, savings, PO compliance, vendor performance, contract renewals, inventory accuracy, asset condition, and capital needs.
* Support annual budgeting and multi-year capital planning through analysis of asset age, condition, repair history, useful life, and total cost of ownership.
* Escalate procurement, vendor, compliance, inventory, or asset risks and recommend corrective action.

**Why should you keep reading and consider working here?**

We know you have other work options, but we ask you to consider working with us at the State of Montana Department of Administration (DOA). Our foundation of success is having effective working relationships, built on mutual trust and respect. We will challenge you to be the best you can be and will work hard to provide a work environment that allows you to succeed. (You can learn more about the DOA here.)

**A Little About Our Business**

The State Procurement Services Division (SPSD) leads best-in-class procurement services through integrity, education, transparency, and innovation. We strive to administer effective and responsible procurements to maximize the value of public funds for Montana.

**What is this career opportunity?**
The Department of Administration's State Procurement Services Division is looking for a Procurement Officer who solves problems and communicates exceptionally well to support the Department of Corrections (DOC).

The State of Montana recently implemented a centralized procurement model built around an enterprise procurement team plus agency-based staff who work alongside the agencies they serve. In this role, you'll be a Department of Administration employee located at DOC, providing procurement support directly to the department. You'll be one of four procurement officers reporting to the DOC procurement supervisor.

You would be responsible for overseeing and coordinating all procurement activities within the DOC ensuring procurements and contracts are completed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with applicable laws, policies, procedures, and funding requirements. This position mentor’s DOC staff in procurement procedures, conducts solicitations for goods and services, and provides contract oversight and management of all assigned and on-going contracts.

If you have good judgment, organizational skills, and the ability to explain complex procurement and contracting requirements to a wide range of internal stakeholders you should apply! We are interested in an individual that is experienced in procurement but also open to someone that is passionate about learning and growing in this role.

Responsibilities Include:

* Develop clear scopes of work, specifications, solicitation documents, evaluation criteria, and contract documentation.
* Conduct market research and analyze pricing, proposals, contract terms, and procurement risk.
* Manage competitive solicitations, evaluations, awards, and contract administration in a fair, transparent, and defensible manner.
* Coordinate contract amendments, renewals, corrective actions, and contract closeout activities.
* Maintain ethical conduct, confidentiality, impartiality, and complete audit-ready procurement files.
* Support procurements essential to Corrections operations, including healthcare, food service, safety and security, technology, and other DOC programs.

*In this position you will be afforded the opportunity to telework, however there will be required weekly in office day(s) in Helena. Specific conditions will be outlined as part of the job offer and must adhere to state policy.*

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Public Administration, Communication, or related field; OR
* Associate degree in Business Public Administration, Communication, or related field and two years’ experience in technical writing, research, or project management; OR
* Alternate combinations of education and experience will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

**Competencies:**

*Ability to:*

* Deliver outstanding customer service
* Conduct research, system analysis, and data gathering analysis
* Prioritize multiple projects and deadlines while working independently in a fast-paced public-sector environment.
* Learn the theory, principles, practices and techniques of government contracting
* Learn the State of Montana's procurement process, administrative rules, and federal procurement rules and laws
* Work and effectively communicate with diverse levels of management and stakeholders
* Establish objectives and priorities based on goals and general direction provided by management
* Identify problems, emerging issues and trends, and establish strategies to address them
* Mediate and resolve disputes
* Work independently with minimal supervision

**Does this sound like you?** Please tell us how and why by submitting your **resume,** **cover letter, and three professional business references.**In your cover letter, please explain why you want to join our team to work in this position. *(Please Note: You do not need to complete the “work experience” or the “education & certifications” portion of the application process in our recruiting system.**You only need to upload the requested documentation.)*

**What can you expect from us in return for your work with our agency?**

+ Receive and relay vendor messages to appropriate staff in an accurate and expedient manner.
+ Key data into Counterpoint within two business days of receiving Purchase Requisitions.
+ Request appropriate approvals prior to issuing Purchase Orders.

Other duties and/or special projects as assigned.

* Proficiency with eVA procurement systems, e-commerce, and inventory management.

Skills:

* Demonstrated skill in using automated procurement systems, e commerce platforms, and inventory management tools.
* Strong attention to detail.
* Strong oral and written communication skills; demonstrated telephone and customer service skills.
* Proficiency with automated purchasing software, MS Word, Excel, and database management.

Abilities:

* Demonstrated ability to process purchase requisitions into purchase orders in accordance with established policies and procedures supporting base supply operations.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret specifications and complete purchase orders in accordance with applicable policies and procedures.
* Ability to work effectively in a high-volume environment.
* Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with vendors and internal end users.

**THE POSITION**
----------------

As a Procurement Contracts Manager with the Budget Division of the Bureau of Fiscal Management, you will take on meaningful work that keeps agency operations moving forward. This role offers a chance to support programs, improve processes, and ensure successful procurement outcomes. You will grow your skills while helping staff navigate complex purchasing needs. Bring your attention to detail and dedication to a position that truly makes a difference.

**DESCRIPTION OF WORK**
-----------------------

This position supports the Department of Revenue by coordinating and completing both routine and complex procurement work. The role helps ensure clear, accurate, and compliant purchasing and contract activities across multiple systems and programs. As a Procurement Contracts Manager, you will perform the following duties:

* **Procurement Coordination:** Coordinate procurement activities, develop documents, and support program offices with accurate and timely guidance
* **Compliance Review:** Review procurement requests and documentation to ensure alignment with laws, directives, and department policies
* **Vendor Communication:** Communicate with vendors to resolve submission issues, clarify requirements, and support smooth procurement processes
* **Record Management:** Maintain procurement records, tracking logs, and system entries to support audits and reporting needs
* **Staff Support:** Provide technical guidance, review documents prepared by others, and assist with onboarding and training new staff
* **Process Improvement:** Support data gathering for cost analysis, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement efforts

Interested in learning more? Additional details regarding this position can be found in the position description.

**Work Schedule and Additional Information:**

* Full-time employment
* Work hours are: Choice of 7:30 AM-4:00 PM with a 60-minute lunch **or** 8:00 AM-4:00 PM with a 30-minute lunch, Monday - Friday.
* **Telework:** You may have the opportunity to work from home (telework) part-time, two days per week in office. In order to telework, you must have a securely configured high-speed internet connection and work from an approved location inside Pennsylvania. If you are unable to telework, you will have the option to report to the headquarters office in Harrisburg. The ability to telework is subject to change at any time. Additional details may be provided during the interview.
* **Salary:**In some cases, the starting salary may be non-negotiable.
* You will receive further communication regarding this position via email. Check your email, including spam/junk folders, for these notices.

**REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, TRAINING & ELIGIBILITY**
-----------------------------------------------

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Minimum Experience and Training Requirements:**

* One year as an Administrative Officer 1; **or**
* Three years of experience in progressively responsible and varied office management or staff work, including experience in personnel management, budgeting, or procurement; and a bachelor's degree; **or**
* Any equivalent combination of experience and training.

**Additional Requirements:**

* You must abide by the prohibition guidelines and refrain from gambling in Pennsylvania casinos, or any casino outside of Pennsylvania with the same owners.
* You must have one year of Commonwealth procurement experience, or three years of non-Commonwealth procurement experience.
* You must be able to perform essential job functions.

**Legal Requirements:**

* This position will have access to Federal Tax Information (FTI) and is subject to the provisions of IRS Publication 1075 (Pub 1075) which requires you to pass an enhanced background check prior to beginning employment. Under Pub 1075, acceptance of a conditional offer of employment will require submission to and approval of satisfactory criminal history reports, including but not limited to: a fingerprint-based federal records check; a PA State Police clearance; a check of local law enforcement agencies where you have lived, worked, and/or attended school within the last five (5) years; and a citizenship/residency verification.

**How to Apply:**

* Resumes, cover letters, and similar documents will **not** be reviewed, and the information contained therein will not be considered for the purposes of determining your eligibility for the position. Information to support your eligibility for the position must be provided on the application (i.e., relevant, detailed experience/education).
* If you are claiming education in your answers to the supplemental application questions, you must attach a copy of your college transcripts for your claim to be accepted toward meeting the minimum requirements. Unofficial transcripts are acceptable.
* Your application must be submitted by the posting closing date*.* Late applications and other required materials will not be accepted.

description:
Make an impact on how Delaware does business. As a State Contract Procurement Officer I, you’ll help shape and manage contracts that support state agencies, schools, local governments, and other public organizations across Delaware. You’ll work with agency partners to develop solicitations, evaluate bids, recommend contract awards, manage existing contracts, and help ensure compliance with state procurement requirements. This is an opportunity to build valuable procurement and contract management expertise while contributing to efficient, responsible use of public resources. If you’re analytical, collaborative, detail-oriented, and ready to grow your career in public procurement, we invite you to apply.

**Essential Functions**
-----------------------

Essential functions are fundamental, core functions common to all positions in the class series and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all job duties for any one position in the class. Since class specifications are descriptive and not restrictive, incumbents can complete job duties of similar kind not specifically listed here.

* Manages existing centralized contracts to ensure compliance with terms of contract; monitors vendor performance and resolves contract disputes, complaints and price discrepancies; negotiates changes.
* Provides consultation services; interprets and explains applicable laws, rules, regulations, policies and procedures for contract development, monitoring, accounting, and auditing.
* Develops, reviews, plans and coordinates procurement activities such as writing bid specifications, developing Request for Proposals (RFP) and Invitations to Bid (ITB), advertising for bid, and recommending contract awards.
* Researches, analyzes and interprets technical aspects of bid specifications for goods and professional and non-professional service contracts.
* Develops proposal criteria in coordination with user agencies.
* Develops contract baselines, terms and conditions through market analysis.
* Conducts pre-bid meetings, facilitates RFP selection committee and participates on related procurement contract committees.
* Negotiates new contracts and contract extensions with vendors using best and final offer techniques and Request for Proposal procedures; recommends contract award, prepares award notice and notifies successful vendors.
* Recommends changes to existing state procurement and contract management processes.

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

**JOB REQUIREMENTS for State Contract Procurement Officer I**

Applicants must have education, training and/or experience demonstrating competence in each of the following areas:

* Six months experience in procurement services which includes purchasing goods and services in accordance with procurement procedures and contract specifications.

* Six months experience in contract management and control which includes ensuring compliance with terms of contracts; negotiating changes to existing contracts.

* Six months experience in interpreting laws, rules, regulations, standards, policies, and procedures.

* Knowledge of developing contracts for procurement of goods and services including researching and writing specifications, analyzing bids and recommending contract award.

**Conditions of Hire**
----------------------

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. The State of Delaware Executive Branch participates in the Federal E-Verify system where the State will provide the federal government with each new hires Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. For more information refer to our job seeker resources.

All new hires are required to report to the **Statewide New Employee Orientation (SNEO)** on their first day of employment. Sessions are held at designated locations in Kent or New Castle County.

**Benefits**
------------

To learn more about the comprehensive benefit package please visit our website at https://dhr.delaware.gov/benefits/

**Selection Process**
---------------------

The application and supplemental questionnaire are evaluated based upon a rating of your education, training and experience as they relate to the job requirements of the position. It is essential that you provide complete and accurate information on your application and the supplemental questionnaire to include dates of employment, job title and job duties. For education and training, list name of educational provider, training course titles and summary of course content. Narrative information supplied in response to the questions must be supported by the information supplied on the application including your employment, education and training history as it relates to the job requirements.

Once you have submitted your application on-line, all future correspondence related to your application will be sent via email. Please keep your contact information current. You may also view all correspondence sent to you by the State of Delawar
